name: 180 Degrees Consulting
description: 180 Degrees Consulting (180DC) is the world’s largest university-based consultancy, providing high-quality consulting services to nonprofits and social enterprises. The UC Merced branch helps organizations solve real-world problems by leveraging student talent in strategy, operations, and technology. Through hands-on experience, members gain valuable consulting skills while making a meaningful social impact.

name: Acts2Fellowship
description: Welcome! Meet A2F - Acts2FellowshipWe are a Christian Fellowship for UC Merced students!Our vision is build an Acts 2 church here at UC Merced. As it says in Acts 2, the disciples shared life in a community devoting themselves to the Bible, prayer, and fellowship in one another's homes.On any given night, we can be getting tacos, playing board games, playing basketball, talking about life, providing mentorship, having study nights with a ton of snacks, studying the bible, etc.We welcome all UC Merced students! Whether you are a believer, a seeker, or just someone interested in hanging out and making some friends - Come check us out!Interested in finding out more?INSTAGRAM: Follow us on Instagram for latest events and updates! https://www.instagram.com/a2f.merced/WEBSITE: Check out our website for more information @ https://a2fmerced.org/EMAIL: Contact us with any questions - acts2merced@gmail.com

name: Actuarial Science Club
description: The Actuarial Science Club (ASC) at UC Merced introduces students to the field of actuarial science and the broader actuary career pipeline, supporting members as they pursue careers in actuarial and related quantitative professions. We help students build foundational skills in statistical analysis, programming, and problem-solving, and connect them to career paths in actuarial science, underwriting, finance, and related fields. Through interviews, panels, and Q&A sessions, members have the opportunity to engage directly with current actuaries and finance professionals, including conferences and webinars hosted in partnership with actuarial and finance companies. ASC also offers resources, study support, and tutoring for students pursuing actuarial exams through the Society of Actuaries (SOA) or Casualty Actuarial Society (CAS), along with hands-on help with statistical and quantitative coursework and hands-on training in tools like Excel, R, and Python through real project work.Whether you're just discovering actuarial science or already on another similar track, ASC is here to help you grow the skills and connections you need to launch a successful career in the field.

name: African Student Union
description: A.S.U. exists to enhance political awareness, cultural awareness, social tolerance, academic success and to provide support for students on campus and in the community. It's "A home away from home" for all the students belonging to the African Diaspora. It's a place where the African culture is celebrated and allows students to be educated on Africa from the food, languages, culture, traditions and history that is not seen in textbooks.

name: Agricultural Insects & Plants
description: The Agricultural Insect and Plants Club  is a﻿ student organization dedicated to exploring the connections between insects, plants, and agriculture through the lens of agroecology and sustainability. Our mission is to provide an inclusive space for learning, research, and community engagement while uplifting underrepresented voices in agricultural and environmental sciences. We host workshops, guest speakers, field visits, and volunteer opportunities with local farms and gardens to foster hands-on experience and community partnerships. We welcomes students from all backgrounds who share an interest in sustainable agriculture, biodiversity, and equity in food systems.

name: AgTech
description: AgTech is an innovative organization designed to connect students passionate about agriculture and technology. It offers a collaborative platform where students can engage with peers who share a common interest in gaining hands-on experience in the field. In partnership with faculty and various departments, AgTech provides students with a "place field"—a dedicated space on the experimental smart farm where they can explore, experiment, and turn their ideas into impactful projects. In addition to working on capstone projects, AgTech also engages in cross-promotion of events with other organizations, encouraging broader collaboration and learning opportunities. This creates a dynamic ecosystem where students can not only immerse themselves in hands-on agriculture tech but also expand their networks and interdisciplinary skills by participating in events and initiatives from other groups on campus.
regularMeetingLocation: UCM Greenhouse/Experimental Smart Farm (Transportation will be provided to site)

name: Alpha Kappa Psi
description: Alpha Kappa Psi is a Co-Ed Business & Professional Fraternity open to all majors founded in 1904 with the purpose of developing its members into principled business leaders. Originally founded by 4 men at New York University, the professional organization now has over 298,000 initiated members at 219 universities in 4 countries. Alpha Kappa Psi has grown to be the oldest and largest business fraternity in the world! With an extensive network of alumni, members are able to land opportunities in a variety of fields at some of the most profitable companies in the world. As one of the best professional co-ed business fraternities, we are truly preparing our brothers for a life of success while creating a strong community with lifelong friendships.

name: Alpha Omega Campus Ministry
description: As a campus ministry, our mission is to create a community safe space for students to learn, talk about, and understand God. This club promotes healthy relationships fostered upon inclusivity and equity. No matter what direction of life you have been walking by, you are welcomed to learn about who God is in our nonjudgmental space. So, if you're looking for a friend to talk to or some cool people to hang with, come join us at one of our fun events!
regularMeetingTime: Mon 7:30pm, Tue 6:30pm, Wed 7:30pm, Friday, Sunday 11 AM

name: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics
description: "One Team, One Dream"The American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA) is a national professional organization built to help aerospace professionals and their organizations succeed. With this, we took this mission to heart and established the UC Merced's AIAA Student Branch in 2013. Since then, our members have grown exponentially fueled by innovative ideas, ambitious energy, and a humble heart. We work on critical projects aimed at providing a well-rounded experience that challenges our members who come from all backgrounds and education. At UC Merced, it is our mission to prepare our members to reach their fullest potential and help launch the next journey of their amazing life. Our members are at the center of what we do at AIAA. Our club provides a diverse portfolio of strategic experiences that offer skill-development opportunities that prepare our members for the professional world. In fact, our Alumni have received offers and now work at some of the top Aerospace Companies in the world. Interested in joining one of our projects? Check out our external website!

name: American Institute of Chemical Engineers at UC Merced
description: We are dedicated to connecting chemical engineers with not only each other but also to resources they can use on their academic and professional journey here at UC Merced. Members will have the opportunity to build their technical and social skills that they will utilize in their future endeavors through social and professional events. At the Chemical Engineering Club, chemical engineers will be able to foster connections with students, faculty, and professionals.

name: American Medical Student Association
description: 1.  Quality, Affordable Healthcare for All      2.  Global Health Equity      3.  Enriching Medicine Through Diversity      4.  Professional Integrity, Development, and Student Well-Being UC Merced AMSA is dedicated to fulfilling both local and national objectives as well as providing information, support, and professional development for future physicians-in-training     1.  To foster intellectual promise, diversity, and community service in the premedical student, while providing benefits and services that aid future physicians-in-training as they prepare for a career in medicine     2.  To create activist leaders in health dedicated to serving the underserved and underrepresented population of the San Joaquin Valley     3.  To inspire students pursuing premedical curricula with a broader perspective, appreciation, and understanding of their chosen major     4.  To establish a peer support group that fosters an environment of camaraderie and guidance to help students avoid the pitfalls and common stressors that accompany the premedical undergraduate career     5.  To provide students with the opportunities to network nationally with other premedical students, medical students, residents, and medical professionalsThese objectives seek to optimize undergraduate candidacy for medical school through work in activism, leadership, research, academic excellence, journalism, tutorship, mentorship, and clinical and non-clinical volunteering.

name: American Red Cross Club
description: We strive to encourage our local community to engage in volunteer work and help others in need. Our purpose is to promote awareness of the American Red Cross services, as well as educate our community about health, safety, disaster preparedness, the importance of blood donations, and much more. We will be guided by the fundamental principles of the American Red Cross and its mission to prevent and alleviate human suffering in the face of emergencies. To do so, we will do our best to mobilize the power of local and student volunteers and the generosity of donors. The American Red Cross Club at UC Merced hopes to learn, practice, and exemplify humanitarian values through Red Cross mission-related service projects.

name: American Society of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
description: We build a community that helps students grow as scientists and pursue opportunities in STEM.

name: American Society Of Civil Engineers Student Chapter at UC Merced
description: The purpose of ASCE shall be to provide resources and general information about a degree in civil engineering and careers related to the major. The goal is to develop a support network for students within the civil engineering program or interested in the major. We aim to create a welcoming community and allow opportunities for students to connect with peers, faculty, and special guests. We will provide resources and workshops for students to improve their academic and professional careers.

name: American Society of Mechanical Engineers at UC Merced
description: The American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) is an international professional organization connecting Mechanical Engineers in the industry and in academia throughout the world. ASME at UC Merced will provide a gateway for UC Merced Mechanical Engineering students to connect with one another, develop their skills and career-readiness, and learn about future professions in the world of Mechanical Engineering. Through professional, technical, and social events, UC Merced students will have the chance to enrich their lives through membership to ASME at UC Merced.

name: Anthropology Society
description: As members of the Anthropology Society, we share a commitment to fostering intellectual curiosity, ethical research, and advancing anthropological knowledge. Our community provides a dynamic platform for dialogue, idea exchange, and cross-disciplinary collaboration. Whether you're a professional, scholar, or enthusiast, join us in exploring the complexities of human existence in anthropology and archaeology. We aim to provide career as well as academic support.

name: Asian American Association
description: The Asian American Association at UC Merced is dedicated to creating an open and welcoming environment for everyone to learn about different Asian American identities and for those of asian heritage to find a sense of belonging. O﻿ur goal is to create a community surrounding Asian American diversity and enhance students’ lifestyles at the university in order to give them new experiences in cultural diversity.

name: Asian Pacific American Medical Student Association UC Merced
description: The Asian Pacific American Medical Student Association (APAMSA) is a national organization of medical and pre-medical students committed to addressing the unique health challenges of Asian American, Native Hawaiian, & Pacific Islander (AANHPI) communities. ?APAMSA serves as a forum for student leaders to engage these health issues and develop initiatives and projects addressing those needs. The local, regional, and national activities of APAMSA aim to promote the health of the AANHPI community and help healthcare workers understand how to care for AANHPI patients in a culturally sensitive manner. Finally, APAMSA provides an important venue for medical students to meet, exchange experiences, and develop personally and professionally through leadership and service.

name: Associated Students of UC Merced
description: Associated Students of UC MercedExecutive Branch Under President Manar Ahmed, elected and appointed student officials provide service to the Undergraduates of UC Merced to have the best suitable student experience. Presiding over the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial Branches, President Ahmed represents the campus to site and system administration whilst assisting each department within our Student GovernmentInternal Vice President CJ Oderinde  presides over the ASUCM Senate, acting as a nonbiased parliamentarian, ensuring all legislative, funding, and bylaw actions are executed. External Vice President Gabriella Martinez connects our campus to outside affiliations, representing ASUCM and UC Merced through the University of California Students’ Association (UCSA), United States Student Association (USSA); reaching to national and international levels. Treasurer Juliana Torres oversees the Budge which includes budget requested RCO's, Departments, and ASUCM Branches + Auxilaries. Working with President Ahmed, a Budget call is hosted each spring to support organizations.Director of Student Activities Victoria De Los Angeles presides over ASUCM affiliated events, community service, outreaches and cultural arts programs. Director De Los Angeles also acts as the Director for ASUCM Auxilary - Campus Activities Board, hosting events on campus such as comedy shows, concerts, or showcases.Legislative - Senate (Wednesdays  - 7:30pm -  KL 232)ASUCM Senate are to be presented by bills or resolutions, voting upon each item whilst receiving unbiased parliamentarianism from Internal Vice President Oderinde. Senate Meetings includes Executive Branch updates, Guest speakers, and presentations of said bills and resolutions. Please refer to the ASUCM website for a list of all senators and their respective positions, in addition to their contact information.Judicial - JusticesASUCM Justices protect the actions brought to and upon ASUCM, able to interpret laws within ASUCM Bylaws using Roberts Rules of order to provide fairness in discussing judicial matters

name: Association for Computing Machinery
description: We are Central Valley’s flagship computer science community at UC Merced! We provide workshops, collaborative projects, mentorship, network, and career advice for Computer Science and many related fields. We currently focus on Software Engineering, Artificial intelligence, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Computer Architecture, and Computer Graphics fields and for each of the fields, we host projects/workshops. If you would like to to boost your resume with projects and get the internships/jobs you want, we welcome you to join our projects and contribute.If you have any interest in Computer Science or would like to meet with other CS students with passion, join ACM. We have General Meetings bi-weekly on Thursdays from 7:30-8:00pm. Please join our discord at bit.ly/acm-ucm-discord and follow our Instagram @ucmacm for latest events and updates.﻿

name: Astronomy Club
description: The Astronomy Club is an undergraduate-run organization at the University of California, Merced. Open to majors and non-majors alike, we strive to provide an educational and fun environment for space enthusiasts. Together with UC Merced astrophysics faculty members, we aim to throw stargazing parties, outreach events, and research opportunities. Join us as we explore the universe together, in a community where everyone's curiosity and enthusiasm are welcomed and encouraged.

name: Ballet Folklórico
description: Since 2007, Ballet Folklórico de UC Merced has continued the tradition to present Folklórico dance and history to the Merced community and uphold the good reputation of the UC Merced Bobcats. The members of Ballet Folklórico de UC Merced seek to increase awareness and the preservation of the dance style of Ballet Folklórico. With this, members of Ballet Folklórico de UC Merced hold workshops that cater to both beginner and advanced dancers to prepare them to work together to give live performances. Furthermore, members of BF de UCM have established this organization to provide, enhance, and support members of Ballet Folklórico de UC Merced who are interested in the different genres of dance that Folklórico has to offer. Our club has been well known for performing dances from the regions of Jalisco, Sinaloa, Nayarit, Veracruz, and Baja California Norte. BF de UCM now offers the region of Nuevo León. As the years go by, it is our hope to add more regions to our setlist to share the beauty within the Mexican culture with our audience.
regularMeetingLocation: Check our Instagram page for practice locations!

name: Bangladeshi Student Association
description: Bangladeshi Student Association (BSA) acknowledges and supports the commitment of the University of California, Merced in creating a safe, inclusive, and welcoming community for all students of diverse qualities and traits.  As a student organization, BSA is mainly focused on working toward the academic and cultural development of Bangladeshi students in various undergraduate and graduate programs at the UC Merced. The major objective of the BSA will be to support and encourage the diverse student community of UC Merced through research and social events, which will significantly help UC Merced to achieve its strategic plan to be the R1 institution. All the members and leaders on the executive team of BSA shall adhere to these commitments in order to keep the membership and the leadership positions.

name: Battery Workforce Challenge
description: Battery Workforce Challenge will provide an immersive, hands-on learning experience for students to gain valuable engineering, manufacturing and battery testing skills that transcend the classroom environment.? The Battery Workforce Challenge is a new three-year student competition that will challenge universities and vocational schools from across North America to design, build, test, and integrate an advanced EV battery pack into a Stellantis vehicle.

name: Bhagat Puran Singh Health Initiative
description: At the core of our organization's mission is a profound commitment to elevating the overall well-being of the Merced and neighboring communities. We go beyond merely providing basic health screenings and fostering general health awareness; we stand as unwavering advocates for social justice initiatives. Our holistic approach recognizes the symbiotic relationship between health and social equity, addressing immediate concerns while actively participating in community-wide efforts to rectify systemic injustices. By catalyzing positive change, we envision a community where healthcare is not just a fundamental right but a cornerstone of social justice. Through collaborative endeavors, we strive to empower individuals, dismantle barriers to health, and cultivate a community rooted in inclusivity, fairness, and compassion.

name: Biophysics Graduate Club
description: Biophysics Graduate Club is an organization of graduate students and postdocs at the University of California, Merced, dedicated to providing exposure to various research topics in biophysics and refining the presentation, writing, and computational skills of its members through a variety of activities. Please find more info on our club website.

name: Bird Seekers and Ornithological Naturalist Group
description: Bird Seekers and Ornithological Naturalist Group (Bird SONG) is a student organization for anyone who's ever heard a bird sing and wondered what species it was or why it was singing. Our mission is to unite people with an interest in birds, birdwatching, and the natural world, fostering a community centered on learning, recreation, opportunity, and exploration.

name: Black Student Coalition
description: The Black Student Coalition's purpose is to provide a safe space for students of the Black and African Diaspora, with an emphasis on mental health and wellness.

name: Black Student Union
description: BSU is comprised of progressive Black students aiming to empower the richness of Black identity, culture, and intellectual heritage.

name: BobCAD
description: The goal of our club is to introduce and prepare students in the STEM pathways for the professional world by giving them an early introduction to Computer Aided Design. We hope to educate students in SolidWorks and lead them to get their CWSA certification.

name: Bobcat Band at UC Merced
description: As one of the oldest clubs on campus, the Bobcat Band is the pride and soul of UC Merced. We demonstrate this with our music and instruments through our three different groups—the Bobcat Band, the Bobcat Orchestra, and The Jazzcats. From within the main Bobcat Band, we play a variety of music, acting as a combination of pep, marching, and concert bands. In addition, we are uniquely the only band program in the entire UC system to be entirely student-led. If you are someone who wants to pick up an instrument for the very first time or are a current musician who wants to play with others at a variety of events, we welcome you to join the Bobcat Band. Throughout our history, we have performed on campus and all around Merced at events such as local city-funded parades, sporting events such as basketball and soccer games, senior homes, and numerous smaller community events. As such, this club will provide a fun and welcoming way to play music not only for yourself, but for the Merced community.
regularMeetingTime: Band: Wednesdays, 7:30 - 10:30 PM | Orchestra: Mondays, 7:30 - 10:00 PM | The Jazzcats: Fridays, 5:00 - 8:00 PM

name: Bobcat Bistro
description: Bobcat Bistro is a cooking club aimed to teach students how to cook, as well as further their cooking skills and to give back to the Merced community. We will provide cooking lessons and other fun activities such as cooking competitions, watching cooking-related movies, and cooking-based games.

name: Bobcat Boxing Club
description: We as the Bobcat Boxing Club at the University of California, Merced, yearn to provide UC Merced students with an entertaining and healthy opportunity to promote self-care through teaching the fundamentals of the art, that is boxing, we establish this constitution and subscribe to the regulations and policies of the University of California, Merced. In the Bobcat Boxing club, we teach basic training and help improve on strength and conditioning.

name: Bobcat Community Builders
description: Bobcat Community Builders is a passionate and dedicated organization founded on the principle of creating positive change within our local community. We are committed to addressing key social issues, including homelessness alleviation, food waste mitigation, and community service, with the belief that together, we can build a better tomorrow.At Bobcat Community Builders, Our Mission is threefold:Homelessness Alleviation: We are committed to providing a helping hand to individuals experiencing homelessness in our community. Through volunteer work, and partnerships with shelters, we strive to provide the support, resources and hope needed to combat homelessness.Food Waste Mitigation: Our dedicated team collaborates with the university, local businesses, restaurants, and food banks to rescue surplus food and redirect it to those who need it most. Plans to host seminars educating students on ways to individually make a difference in their carbon footprint.Community Service: We understand that the strength of our community lies in the collective effort of its members. Bobcat Community Builders offers a variety of community service opportunities for volunteers to engage with their neighbors.

name: Bobcat Law School Admissions Test Preparation and Studying Club
description: We are The Bobcat Law School Admissions Test Preparation and Studying Club. Our club meets weekly for an hour to focus on the Law School Admission Test (LSAT). Meetings include learning what the LSAT is, exploring key strategies, concepts, ‘tools’, and recurring themes as well as practicing together and sharing experiences. All materials used or claims made are drawn from reputable sources and presented in an objective, paraphrased format. In addition to academic preparation, the club provides a space to compare LSAT prep courses, costs, and student preferences, helping members make informed decisions. In short, we seek to serve and help the Pre-Law community prepare and study for the pivotal Law School Admission Test.

name: Bobcat Magica
description: Bobcat?Magica (BCM) is UC Merced’s inclusive hub for all things Japanese pop culture! We celebrate anime, manga, games, and more through discussions, screenings, creative activities, and fun events. Our mission is to create a welcoming space—especially for new fans and female-identifying fans—where everyone can share their passions, make friends, and explore the vibrant world of J-pop culture together.

name: Bobcat Mock Trial
description: Bobcat Mock Trial is a club that teaches students about the American legal system through trial simulations and participation in Mock Trial competitions. Members will learn about the legal process, practices, and procedures, as well as obtain coaching from the Chief Deputies of the Merced County DA's office. Members will prepare for a full trial at the end of the semester conducted in front of various legal professionals from across the state, in addition to competing in the American Mock Trial Associations' collegiate competition circuit.

name: Bobcat Model United Nations
description: Confidence - Leadership  - DebateModel United Nations  is UCM's speech and debate club that lets students step into the shoes of the most powerful people in history. We represent the interests of the countries of the world  in our weekly general meetings, and compete nationally head-on against the world's top universities in elegant debate halls.CAMPUS WEEKLY MEETINGS: Every week, we host a session on real-world issues, handwritten and researched   by our members. We'll assign you a country or a character to represent.With your solo speeches to the room, negotiates in free-for-all discussion, and legislative writing skill for the final bill, you must sway the opinion of the room to benefit your agenda. Most bills need >50% of the vote to pass; ALLY with  like-minded powerful people, SABOTAGE your enemies , and INSPIRE the undecided masses to believe your bill is the one true ideology.We do a mix  of serious and fun sessions, set throughout the course of history, ranging from modern topics concerning international disputes to famous historical conflicts, to occasional fun topics on our favorite hobbies and fandoms.NATIONAL COMPETITIONS:We compete at New York University, UC Berkeley, USC, Santa Barbara, and this year, the University of Chicago. The best part? Your travel costs are paid for. Bring success to UC Merced as you verbally spar against the members of top colleges to influence world policy. We attend FOUR competitions a year, and host tryouts for every one.TRYOUTS: Passionate attendees can contact president Saman at sbajpai2@ucmerced.edu to research a topic to defend on tryout day. The criteria includes not only your speaking and argumentative skills, but how well you carry yourself, analyze history, and write powerful messages.We always reserve spots on the travel team for first-timers.

name: Bobcat Runnings Run Club
description: Bobcat Runnings Run Club is a co-ed student organization at UC Merced dedicated to bringing students together through a shared passion for running, community, and personal growth. Our primary purpose is to provide students with a welcoming “third space” where they can meet new people, socialize, and build meaningful connections outside of the classroom.Bobcat Runnings welcomes students of all running backgrounds and experience levels, from beginners who are just getting started to experienced runners looking to improve. We aim to create a safe, supportive, and inclusive environment where everyone feels comfortable participating at their own pace.Through group runs, social activities, and opportunities to connect with fellow students, our club encourages members to become better runners while also developing confidence, friendships, discipline, and a strong sense of community. Ultimately, Bobcat Runnings strives to make running an enjoyable and accessible experience while inspiring our members to become better runners and better people

name: BobCat Wind Club
description: The Bobcat Wind Club is a student-led engineering and renewable energy organization at the University of California, Merced, dedicated to representing our university in the Collegiate Wind Competition (CWC+).Our mission is to bring together students from diverse academic backgrounds to collaborate, innovate, and develop practical solutions to real-world renewable energy challenges. Through this national competition, our team aims to design, construct, and test a functional wind turbine prototype while exploring the technical, economic, and environmental aspects of wind energy development.Beyond engineering, the Bobcat Wind Club emphasizes community engagement, sustainability, and education. We strive to make a meaningful impact by promoting renewable energy awareness, connecting with industry professionals, and inspiring future generations through STEM outreach.Our club welcomes students from all majors, including mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, environmental science, business, and communications. No previous wind energy experience is required—just curiosity, dedication, and a willingness to learn.Our goal is to proudly represent UC Merced on the national stage, gain hands-on experience, develop future leaders in renewable energy, and demonstrate the impact that Bobcats can make in advancing a sustainable energy future.

name: Bobcats on Broadway
description: would you like to be a part of a theater organization on campus geared towards performing known plays, musicals, and student written pieces for the public?Then, you're in the right place! Contact:Instagram: @bobcatsonbroadwayEmail: bobcatsonbroadway@gmail.com

name: Campus 2 Community Outreach
description: C2C Outreach empowers college students to bridge the gap between campus and underserved communities through compassionate, healthcare education. We are committed to delivering medical outreach, health education, and advocacy to vulnerable populations while cultivating the next generation of community-engaged healthcare leaders.

name: Campus Activities Board
description: The Campus Activities Board (CAB) was created to provide a variety of entertainment, co-curricular programming and social activities for the student body at UC Merced in order to create a social network and community that will enhance the development of character and scholarship amongst students.CAB is currently under the direction of ASUCM's Student Director of Student Activities Stephanie Madrigal and Vice Chair Isaac Munoz. For information about future events or about joining the Campus Activities Board, contact our advisor JaeJae Julian. UC Merced's Campus Activities Board past events include CABapalooza, CABCinema, Drag Queen Bingo, Treats N' Beats, Bobcats Got Talent, CAB Ball, Dance Off, CABsterical, and Cowtopia! We incorporate Passion, Hospitality, Innovation, and Leadership into our events!

name: Campus Advocacy, Resources and Education
description: The Campus Advocacy, Resources, and Education (CARE) office collaborate with UC Merced partners to develop and support an understanding of gender-based violence through prevention education and trauma-informed care advocacy using an intersectional framework.

name: Campus Compass
description: Campus Compass is a professional organization aimed at providing guidance, support, and advice by pairing college 1st years up with seasoned students to navigate their path through college and beyond.

name: Cat Court (Moot Court of UC Merced)
description: Bobcat Moot Court is committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse environment where all students, regardless of background, have an equal opportunity to participate. Our club is dedicated to engaging underrepresented voices on campus while ensuring that every student can explore the world of appellate advocacy. Open to students of all years and majors, we provide a space for those interested in legal reasoning, persuasive argumentation, and courtroom procedure to develop their skills and connect with legal professionals.

name: Catholic Newman Club
description: We are a student run organization for Catholics, spanning across every university in the nation. Our goals is strengthening students faith, while nourishing their pursuit of higher education. As well, helping create life long bonds with other students that help one become a better Christian.

name: Chemists Who Care
description: Chemists Who Care is an all-inclusive, progressive organization aiming to make science education accessible to all and to support positive change in the community. Chemists Who Care is founded on principles of empathy, integrity, and community service. Chemists Who Care welcomes all students, regardless of major, to participate in it’s goal of making real change in the Merced and UCM community

name: Chess Club
description: The Chess Club at UCM envisions bringing together the chess community on campus by providing a place for players of all skill levels, backgrounds, and majors to play and learn.

name: Chi Alpha: Merced Christian Fellowship
description: We believe, expect, and experience the love of God through His truth, His people, His miracles, and the gifts of the Holy Spirit. We are focused on transforming our world locally and around the globe through receiving and releasing the supernatural life of God. We are focused on reaching and equipping ethnically diverse students in the campus community to love and embrace diverse ethnicities with an expressed focus on an international student community that best represents the Kingdom of God.

name: Chinese Cultural Club
description: Welcome to the Chinese Cultural Club! Our club's purpose is to share the Chinese culture and traditions to our fellow peers. Our club is scheduled to meet once every week. New activities will happen every week, examples include: playing Chinese games (Mafia, Detecting the Murderer), watching Chinese cartoons (with eng sub), and learning about the ancient history of China. In addition, we provide space and support for those interested in learning the Chinese language. The fun is here! The knowledge is here! Your new friends are also here!

name: Choir Club
description: Welcome to the Choir Club! Our goal is to provide a space for students to express themselves through vocal music and foster a community surrounding a shared interest.

name: Cognitive Science Student Association
description: The members of CSSA strive to support Cognitive Science majors, minors, and enthusiasts in various aspects of academia by organizing study groups, topic seminars, projects, workshops, and an annual conference trip. Connections to field-related opportunities, such as research assistant positions that may bridge into real-world occupations.

name: College Democrats at UC Merced
description: The College Democrats at UC Merced's missions is to get democrat officials elected at the local state and federal levels. This is achieved by uplifting members of  our community and advocating for those who are in need. We, the members of the College Democrats at UC Merced, established to provide students at the University of California, Merced the means for promoting Democratic policies and the general interests of the Democratic Party,The College Democrats at UC Merced pledge themselves to support the philosophy and candidates of the Democratic Party. CDUCM shall strive to provide students with the means for promoting Democratic policies & and the general interests of the Democratic Party. UCMDEMS shall also seek to promote voter awareness on campus, in an attempt to increase voter turnout among students.

name: Community Campus Garden
description: The purpose of the Community Campus Garden to provide students with volunteering opportunities, as well as gardening and sustainability skills. Every other week, produce is harvested and donated to the Food Pantry on campus.

name: Community Engagement Center
description: The Community Engagement Center brings together UC Merced students, staff, faculty, and Merced community members, agencies, and organizations to create and develop reciprocal partnerships that generate student learning, build capacity, and solve problems through service, scholarship, and leadership. These actions contribute to building a healthy and sustainable community (local to global) and creating positive change. The Community Engagement Center strives to:Facilitate equitable, effective, and reciprocal partnerships and opportunities for students, faculty, and community partners in educational and co-curricular service and research experiences.Provide opportunities to, and facilitate connections between, campus and community entities.Support positive community engagement outcomes through educational workshops, trainings, and program implementation.ON WEDNESDAYS, CEC CLOSES AT 7:30 PM, not 5 PM!

name: Cosplay-Cats at UC Merced
description: The UC Merced Cosplay Club is a welcoming and creative community for students who share an interest in cosplay, costumes, fandoms, and self-expression. Our goal is to build a supportive community where people who have experience with cosplay can connect with others, while also welcoming anyone who is interested in learning how to cosplay or trying it for the first time The club provides opportunities for members to meet new people, share their creativity, learn cosplay skills, participate in activities and events, and celebrate the characters and fandoms they love. Whether you are an experienced cosplayer, someone who has always wanted to try cosplay, or simply interested in the community, everyone is welcome. We strive to create an inclusive and respectful environment where members can express themselves, make friends, and enjoy cosplay together.

name: Crochet Club
description: The purpose of this organization is to provide the University of California, Merced, with a club centered around crocheting that is not currently available to the students that attend the school. CCUCM will provide a way to express oneself through crocheting while also helping the community through donations and fundraisers. The organization will also teach crocheting to those who are new to the activity while providing a space for anyone to come and crochet.

name: Data Science Society
description: The Data Science Society at UC Merced is a student-led organization dedicated to fostering a collaborative community for those interested in data science, machine learning, and analytics. Whether you are simply interested in data science or want to explore the field more deeply, we have something for everyone. We host workshops, guest talks, and project-based learning opportunities to help members develop practical skills, explore real-world applications, and connect with peers and industry professionals. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced coder, our goal is to make data science accessible, engaging, and impactful for all.

name: Delta Delta Delta
description: Tri Delta is an assembly of women with shared values where you can be yourself and belong to something bigger. We are brave,bold and kind. We are passionate about serving others, committed to becoming the best version of ourselves and dedicated tohelping women live, learn and lead—with Purpose—for a lifetime.

name: Delta Epsilon Mu
description: The Members of the Theta Chapter of Delta Epsilon Mu, Inc. at the University of California, Merced shall remain committed to providing a professional environment for students who are seeking a future in a professional field of health. As a Student Organization, the Theta Chapter shall strive to establish a network of connections between Active Members, Alumni Members, professors, and health care professionals. This network shall exist to further develop professional skills of the Members, to unite the health community, and to promote community awareness of health-related topics through health education.The Members of the Theta Chapter of Delta Epsilon Mu, Inc. at the University of California, Merced are dedicated to serving the community and uniting students of diverse backgrounds with interest in the varying health fields through leadership, professional development, and brotherhood. The Chapter shall be organized and operated exclusively for charitable and educational purposes within the meaning of Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the “Code”).

name: Delta Gamma
description: Membership in Delta Gamma brings with it countless memories and experiences which will shape its members for years to come. Consistent with our Founders' thoughts in 1873, our primary purpose is to create an environment for our members in which lasting friendships and our vows of sisterhood emanate all aspects of our Fraternity. We encourage an atmosphere that will foster high ideals of friendship among college women, promote their educational and cultural interests, create in them a true sense of social responsibility and develop in them high qualities of character. Delta Gamma is more than just a collegiate experience; it is a lifetime of commitment with support and opportunity awaiting you. It marks the beginning of a relationship that will last, not just four years, but for a lifetime.

name: Delta Sigma Pi
description: Delta Sigma Pi is the nation’s leading co-ed professional business fraternity, with a commitment to equipping our members throughout their careers to make a greater impact in their business, civic, and personal lives. Recognized as America's best business fraternity, Delta Sigma Pi attracts members from all backgrounds and walks of life. Delta Sigma Pi is a professional fraternity organized to foster the study of business in universities; to encourage scholarship, social activity and the association of students for their mutual advancement by research and practice; to promote closer affiliation between the commercial world and students of commerce, and to further a higher standard of commercial ethics and culture and the civic and commercial welfare of the community.We strive to uphold our core values of professional development, diversity and ethics, service and philanthropy, leadership, and social. The Fraternity also designates national service initiatives, which currently are Ronald McDonald House Charities and Make A Difference Day.Only students matriculating in a qualified program in the University of California, Merced majoring in Management Business Economics, or Economics shall be eligible to election in this Fraternity as a member.

name: Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated
description: Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated is an organization of college educated women committed to the constructive development of its members and to public service with a primary focus on the Black community. It is a private, not-for-profit organization whose purpose is to provide assistance and support through established programs in local communities throughout the world. The Phi Alpha Chapter of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated is the first National Pan-Hellinc Council  "Divine Nine" organization chartered at the University of California, Merced on November 18th, 2023.

name: Dermatology and Health Sciences Association
description: The Dermatology and Health Sciences club at UC Merced aims to provide students with the opportunity to learn about skin health, overall health, healthcare professions of all types, raise awareness about common dermatological/systemic issues , and promote good wellness practices. We seek to support the community by offering resources, hosting educational events, and facilitating volunteer opportunities for those interested in pursuing dermatology or getting immersed into many other healthcare professions. We aim to further develop our scientific mind and critical thinking skills by staying up to date on modern scientific papers and supporting everyone on their academic and professional journeys in healthcare and the health sciences. Through collaboration and outreach, we strive to enhance the overall well-being of our peers while fostering a deeper understanding of overall health and wellness of the human body, which includes skin.

name: Diva Stride Run Club
description: Diva Stride is an all-girls run club dedicated to empowering women through fitness, friendship, and community. We’re all about creating a safe, judgment-free space where every girl feels supported — whether you're a seasoned runner or just starting out.Our mission is to unite women on campus through movement, promote healthy lifestyles, and build meaningful connections that go beyond the classroom. From weekly group runs around campus to showing up at local 5Ks in matching fitness sets, Diva Stride is about showing up for yourself — and each other.We also host empowering events and fundraisers, including efforts to support breast cancer awareness. Every stride we take is a step toward confidence, community, and positive change.Join us and find your stride — because every diva deserves to shine. 💖👟

name: Diversified Doctors
description: Our organization is dedicated to informing undergraduate pre-med students about the process of becoming a doctor and providing opportunities that allow these students to diversify the medical field with their unique ideas. We pride ourselves on founding this organization for active participation of our members, who will gain not only information on the pre-med process, but also experience in skills that will help them become a doctor. We strive to be a successful, student-led, non-profit organization that engages individuals to promote equal opportunity to medical school through research, outreach, and innovation.

name: Dungeons and Dragons Club
description: The Dungeons and Dragons club is an organization that helps students relax and socialize through the world of D&D. Dungeons and dragons, for those who do not know, is a roleplaying game where a group of people get together and immerse themselves in a fantastical world. The game is run by the DM (Dungeon Master), while the rest of the group consist of players who play characters that adventure through wondrous, impactful, and often dangerous worlds. We welcome all members, whether they are new or experienced players, and are always looking to make new events for club members to enjoy. Meetings for the club are from 6pm - 8:30pm on Tuesdays. The Fall 2026 meeting location is Glacier 150. These meetings, members can play D&D as well as other various types of tabletop games. They also work as a negotiation time, for those who cannot make the whole meeting, to plan out when they can play the game. Many people have made friendships and bonds over playing D&D, our club's goal is to help as many members as possible. We have a free to play environment, and have experienced players and resources ready to help anybody at anytime. The main communication for this club is through discord. Here is the link: https://discord.gg/7gZd8xJmun.

name: East African Student Association
description: The East African Student Association’s mission is to promote and share East African culture within the University of California, Merced community. We strive to educate and empower students, fostering a sense of community and solidarity. By highlighting our diverse traditions, we aim to create an inclusive environment for African students and engage the entire student body in experiencing the richness of our cultures.Through a variety of events and collaborations, EASA seeks to strengthen connections among students and the wider community. Our goal is to create lasting relationships, elevate awareness of East African heritage, and celebrate diversity on campus. As we grow, we're committed to increasing the visibility and impact of our cultural presence at UC Merced.

name: Economics Club
description: We provide members with class help, careers, and internship resources! We hope these resources are useful. The UCM Economics Club is an Academic organization that brings together those who have a interest in economics. Students from any major can attend! Our main goal is to provide information that is valuable and to provide insight from experts in the field. You get to decide what is valuable; we will do the hard work to acquire the best information for our members.Meeting time and dates are to be determined per semester

name: El Club de Español
description: El Club de Español, best known as ECE/ECEDEUCM, is an organization created for all the people who feel the need to reconnect to their cultural roots. However, it is open to people of all ethnicities that are passionate by the Spanish language as well as their native language. The main purpose of ECE is to make all the members feel as if they’re in a family environment, even away from their own communities. ECE provides the members the power and freedom to express themselves with Spanish, Hispanic cultures, Latin American music, dance, art and literature learned through the club and Spanish classes.  El Club de Español is an organization that wants to promote education and unity at UC Merced and there is no intention to create or promote inequality between UC Merced students. We want to bring students together with language, culture, education, and similar experiences.

name: Experiential Learning
description: Experiential Learning (EL) at UC Merced is a campus-wide initiative that empowers Bobcats to move beyond theory and apply their education in real-world settings. Coordinated through the Division of Student Affairs, the initiative integrates hands-on education across academic disciplines to help students build career-ready skills, establish professional networks, and create measurable change on campus and across the Central Valley.Five Pillars of Experiential Learning: Community Service & Civic Engagement: Direct volunteerism, community-based projects, and structured fellowships,such as College Corps and Bright Sparks Scholars, that address regional needs in literacy, education, public health, and sustainability. Student Leadership: Practical cohort workshops, accelerator seminars (IGNITE, EMPOWER), and outdoor immersion through the Yosemite Leadership Program that build executive, communication, and inclusive leadership skills. Undergraduate Research: Faculty-mentored scholarly inquiry and funded lab fellowships through the Undergraduate Research Opportunities Center (UROC)—including SURI, SOAR, and UC LEADS—culminating in academic symposia and research conferences. Internships & Professional Practice: Applied career experiences with industry leaders, public agencies, and campus units, supported by specialized programs like the UC Washington Program (UCDC) and UC Center Sacramento (UCCS).Global Learning & Study Abroad: Immersive international coursework, sister-campus summer programs, and global field research through UCEAP that build cross-cultural competencies.

name: Fashion Forward at UC Merced
description: Fashion Forward at UC Merced is committed to advancing equitable practices and sustainability in fashion. This organization will utilize student-education efforts and campus initiatives to promote inclusivity and representation of underserved and minority communities, highlight sociocultural implications behind artistic expressions, as well as educate on ethical and responsible consumption practices. Fashion Forward at UC Merced strives to empower students, faculty, and alumni to foster a greener and socially responsible future.

name: Financial Wellness Center
description: The Financial Wellness Center at UC Merced was founded in 2020, with the goal of assisting students to develop and achieve financial wellness by creating a safe and inclusive environment for students to discuss and learn more about their own personal financial management.

name: First Generation Collective
description: Our organization is a supportive community for first-generation students who are navigating college for the first time. We create a space where students can connect and feel a sense of belonging at UC Merced. Through social events, academic and professional workshops, and peer support, we help members prepare for life during and after college. Our goal is to make the college experience feel less overwhelming and more empowering.

name: Fraternity and Sorority Council
description: The Fraternity and Sorority Council, hereafter referred to as FSC, shall be the governing body for all recognized social fraternities and sororities at the University of California, Merced. The purpose of this council is to maintain the system of our FSC-affiliated chapters, connect the FSC chapters in their individual points of action, support the recruitment of new members to FSC chapters, build relationships and networks between its FSC chapters, support mutual efforts of fundraising by the FSC chapters, and provide professional opportunities to the members of the FSC chapters, general student body, and community at large. Panhellenic Sororities: ¦      Delta Delta Delta, Delta Gamma, Kappa Kappa Gamma, Phi MuNALFO Fraternities and Sororities:¦      Kappa Delta Chi Sorority, Inc., Lambda Theta Nu Sorority, Inc.Multicultural Sorority: ¦      Sigma Theta Psi Multicultural Sorority, Inc. NIC-affiliated fraternities:¦      Kappa Sigma, Pi Kappa Phi, Omega Delta Phi Fraternity, Inc., Sigma Chi

name: Fraternity and Sorority Life
description: Fraternity & Sorority Life exists to enhance the collegiate experience through leadership, scholarship, service, and social development. Fraternity & Sorority Life will also serve to educate on the positive nature and goals of Greek Life, while building unity through the creation of strong and lasting relationships. These standards shall promote personal and civic responsibilities as well as give back to the university and surrounding community.We value...ScholarshipLeadershipServiceFriendshipCommitment to Social JusticeLeadershipThe leadership opportunities and training within a fraternity or sorority help to prepare its members for the future by developing responsibility and character.ScholarshipThe scholarship focus and emphasis on academic excellence encourages members to realize their purpose for attending the university — to achieve higher education and to become more knowledgeable about scholarly subjects and the world around them.ServiceThe service shown to the campus or community through direct volunteer and philanthropic contributions humbles fraternity or sorority members. It also strengthens a sense of accomplishing something for the good of others.FriendshipThe lifelong bonds of friendship created within a fraternity or sorority help to keep its members unified in achieving a common goal.

name: Future Industrial Organizational Psychologists
description: The purposes of this organization shall be: To promote awareness and understanding of the field of Industrial-Organizational Psychology among students through informational sessions, outreach activities, and educational programming, to provide members with academic and professional development opportunities related to Industrial-Organizational Psychology, including but not limited to simulated and applied practice of I/O-related work, skill development activities, and potential partnerships with businesses or organizations, to support members in preparation for graduate education in Industrial-Organizational Psychology and related fields by offering guidance on graduate program selection, application processes, and academic planning, including course scheduling aligned with graduate school expectations, to foster a supportive academic and professional community that encourages collaboration, mentorship, and engagement among students with shared interests in Industrial-Organizational Psychology, to enhance members’ exposure to the field through guest speakers, workshops, and professional presentations, to raise funds as necessary to support organizational activities, events, and programming consistent with the purposes of the organization, to operate as a non-profit student organization.
regularMeetingTime: Every 2 weeks on Thursday from 5:00 PM- 6:00 PM

name: Game Ain't Based of Sympathy
description: I want to create an Esports Club at UC Merced that brings students together through competitive and casual gaming. The goal of this club is to build a strong gaming community on campus where students can connect, collaborate, and showcase their skills in a positive and inclusive environment. The club will host regular practice sessions, tournaments, and tryouts to identify top players who can represent UC Merced in intercollegiate esports competitions against other universities. In addition to competition, the club will promote teamwork, strategic thinking, leadership, and sportsmanship. By establishing an organized esports program, UC Merced can create opportunities for students to engage socially, relieve stress, and take pride in representing their school in the growing world of collegiate esports.

name: Game Development Club
description: The Game Development Club at UC Merced is a club aimed at students who have any interest in game development, hobby or career. Any skill level is welcome, whether you're just getting started with game development or if you've made many in the past, along with any discipline! We primarily exist on Discord, so join us at: https://discord.gg/GJY7X2V3A6

name: Global Med Collective
description: The Global Med Collective at UC Merced is dedicated to empowering students pursuing careers in healthcare by providing essential resources, mentorship, and community support. Our mission is to increase representation in medicine, reduce health disparities affecting Black and Brown communities, and promote health equity. Through educational workshops, professional development events, and community outreach, we aim to prepare our members for successful careers in medicine and public health. We also foster a strong network of support, ensuring that members can connect, grow, and inspire one another as future leaders in healthcare. Whether through peer mentorship, advocacy initiatives, or collaborations with healthcare professionals, the Global Med Collective Organization is committed to uplifting our community and advancing opportunities for students passionate about making a meaningful difference in the health fields.

name: Google Developer Group on Campus: UC Merced
description: Google Developer Group on Campus: UC Merced, supported by Google Developers, invites university students from all backgrounds to connect, learn, and grow through all things Google, from TensorFlow to Google Cloud to Android! Anyone can join to improve their technical repertoire in a collaborative and open environment, all while building solutions for their local community.Join us on Discord!ConnectMeet students interested in developer technologies at UC Merced. All are welcome, including those with diverse backgrounds and different majors. There's something for everyone, from marketing to cloud computing to outreach!LearnLearn about a range of technical topics and gain new skills through hands-on workshops, events, talks, and project-building activities - both online and in-person.GrowApply new skills to solve local problems; advance your career and network; and give back to your community by helping others learn.

name: Grad Nomads
description: Grad Nomads is a student-led community built around two things: connection and growth. We're here for international graduate students at UC Merced first and foremost, but our doors are open to the whole graduate student body, because grad school is better when we're not doing it alone.Whether international or domestic, everyone committed to our mission is welcome to be part of the community we're building together.We bring people together through two main pillars:  Community      Building      We build community through friendly gatherings, cross-cultural      celebrations, and casual meetups. Whether it's a coffee break or a      cultural celebration, there's always a space to connect, unwind, and be      reminded you're not on this journey alone.              Professional      Development      We help you think beyond the dissertation — networking events, career      panels, and workshop-style sessions to help you navigate academia and      beyond, with guidance from peers and professionals inside and outside UC      Merced. Above all, Grad Nomads is a small, informal, and welcoming space where grad students can ask questions, share experiences, and grow together. Join us. Bring your culture, your questions, and your curiosity. As a small global community at UC Merced, we're here to make grad school feel a little less lonely and a lot more joyful.

name: Graduate Pedagogy Association
description: The Graduate Pedagogy Association (GPA) is a graduate student organization founded in 2016 to support aspiring educators at UC Merced. As a cooperative supplementation, GPA offers pedagogy-based assistance to graduate students that may fall outside the scope of staff-led campus organizations. GPA’s mission is to assist the pedagogical development of both novice and experienced TAs and educators by equipping them with simple yet effective resources to enhance their teaching practices. We accomplish this goal by utilizing a multifaceted approach to skill development, including workshops with practical, instance-based training, guest faculty speakers, and peer-led discussions. Additionally, aside from GPA’s agenda, we work closely with other organizations on campus, including the Center for Engaged Teaching and Learning (CETL), to give back to the larger academic community by assisting with other on-campus events.

name: Ground State
description: To provide a forum for graduate and postdoctoral students from the Chemistry and Biochemistry department to come together for academic, community service and social activities at the University of California Merced. In this club, all graduate students and postdocs from the CBC department can meet each other, ask each other for advice and mentor each other.This club aims at organizing at least one professional development workshop for the graduate students and one social event so that incoming students and postdocs get to meet everyone each semester. Easy communication through the Slack Ground State group (email us to be added)

name: HackMerced
description: HackMerced is a 36-hour annual hackathon that occurs at the University of California, Merced, and is open to students from all over the world. During the event, participants will collaborate in teams, build a project, and attend workshops to learn about new technologies.

name: Health Promotion
description: The mission of the Health Promotion Department is to foster a campus community that encourages positive health behaviors supportive of UC Merced students' academic success and well-being during their collegiate experience.  This is achieved by using available data and following a primary prevention philosophy in our efforts to provide health education, train student leaders, advocate for change, and promote health equity.

name: Healthy Food Association
description: The Healthy Food Association goal is to provide education on Healthy Food alternatives to students who are on a budget at UC Merced, hold fundraisers to raise funds for the local food pantry in Merced, and create a pathway to volunteer at the local food pantry.

name: Hearts for Hope
description: Hearts for Hope is a student organization at UC Merced dedicated to supporting children affected by cancer and other illnesses. Through acts of kindness, community service, awareness initiatives, and fundraising, we strive to bring comfort, joy, and hope to children and their families during difficult times.Our organization allows students to make a meaningful difference through activities such as creating handmade cards, bracelets, gifts, and care packages, organizing donation drives, and supporting charities and organizations that help children facing serious illnesses. We also aim to raise awareness and build partnerships that extend our impact beyond campus.At Hearts for Hope, we believe that even the smallest acts of kindness can make a difference. By bringing together students who share a passion for helping others, we hope to remind every child we reach that they are cared for, supported, and never forgotten. Together, we strive to bring a little more hope into the lives of children and families who need it most.

name: Hermanas Unidas
description: Hermanas Unidas is a diverse group of individuals that strives to support Chicanx womxn in higher education through social, academic, and community service events. Our powerful and passionate space is designed to be inviting to individuals of all backgrounds. We live by our motto “Poder De La Mujer”, a statement that affirms and empowers that womxn have the strength to pursue anything they set their mind to. Please join our meetings at any time during the semester. "Once an Hermana, Always an Hermana." We will meet weekly on Thursday's @ 7:30 in COB 114. We hope to see you there!

name: Hmong Student Association
description: Hmong Student Association (HSA) is an undergraduate organization formed on campus by the Hmong-college going community of UC Merced. In the Hmong Student Association, the student's pride themselves in promoting Hmong culture, heritage, and language within the UC Merced Community by celebrating students pursuing higher education, knowledge, and skills. Together, the students will showcase their talents through cultural performances such as dance, song, and story-telling and through historical lessons through our spoken language.

name: Homebound Dance Team
description: Homebound Dance Team is a non-profit student organization that emphasizes awareness and development of dance through educational and social means within the Central Valley. We aim to group people together to perform sets at various events throughout the year, fostering a strong community of dancers from any and all backgrounds.

name: Horror Club
description: Do you like scary movies? Do you have nothing to do in your dorm? Well come out and watch some of your favorite horror movies, dress comfortable and bring snacks and blanket

name: Ice Cream and Baking Club
description: The purpose of this organization is to allow students to get to know people and to relax from any outside stress that you may have. Being able to get together with friends and other students would be a fun, short-term escape from other responsibilities. We wanted to create a safe space where one can have fun and enjoy yourself, while baking treats and pairing it with ice cream! Hopefully you consider joining!

name: Ice Hockey Club at UC Merced
description: Ice Hockey Club at UC Merced is a student-led organization dedicated to growing the game of ice hockey at UC Merced by providing students with opportunities to play, learn, compete, and build a strong campus community.Our mission is to create an inclusive environment where students of all experience levels can enjoy hockey. Whether you're an experienced player, completely new to the sport, or simply a fan looking to get involved, everyone is welcome. The club offers organized practices, games against other colleges and teams, skill development, and opportunities to build lifelong friendships through a shared passion for hockey.Beyond the ice, members can participate in social events, volunteer opportunities, community outreach, and team-building activities that strengthen leadership, sportsmanship, and school spirit. As we continue to grow, our goal is to establish a sustainable and competitive hockey program that proudly represents UC Merced while making the sport more accessible to students across campus.The Ice Hockey Club at UC Merced is committed to fostering teamwork, personal growth, and a welcoming community where members can challenge themselves, create lasting memories, and help shape the future of hockey at UC Merced.

name: Ignition Automotive Club
description: The purpose(s) of this organization shall be to fester and grow interest in students as well as provide them opportunities in automotive engineering, and provide valuable knowledge about vehicles and motorsports. The intended impact of the organization on the University is to give students a better understanding of applying what they learn in class to an appliance they see everyday, and provide students the chance to grow their creativity and automotive skills in different activities. The services provided are social bonding, understanding the multitude of aspects of a car, and growing creativity in engineering design.

name: Immigrant ROOTS - Rising Organizers for Opportunity, Transformation, and Solidarity
description: ROOTS is a chapter of the organization, United We Dream, which is the largest immigrant youth-led organization in the country that aims to fight to advance the rights of immigrant families and students at the local, federal level & educational system. Over the years, we’ve led actions for the Dream Act, Gaithersburg Freedom City, the Supreme Court School Walkouts, and many more. The purpose of this campus organization shall be to create resources and inform students about social justice issues affecting their community and is committed to advocating for education, immigration, women, and LGBTQ+ rights, among other intersectional groups. The chapter will create a welcoming environment for undocumented students through education, support, and empowerment. Undocu Pride at UC Merced, will be an extension of the United We Dream non-profit organization at the University. The intended impact of the organization on the University community is to bring more resources, support, and advocacy to students.

name: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
description: We are a student branch of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers. Our mission is to connect the students of UC Merced with IEEE resources and events, working on electronics-based projects, and collaborating with other STEM organizations on campus. Open to all majors on campus.

name: InterVarsity Christian Fellowship
description: InterVarsity is a vibrant campus ministry that establishes and advances witnessing communities of students and faculty.The purpose of InterVarsity Christian Fellowship at UC Mercedis to establish and advance at colleges and universities witnessing communities of students and faculty who follow Jesus as Savior and Lord: growing in love for God, God’s Word, God’s people of every ethnicity and culture, and God’s purposes in the world.

name: Investment Club
description: The Investment Club at UC Merced is a student-run organization focused on collaborative, project-driven investing and financial initiatives. Rather than operating as a classroom or lecture-based club, we bring students together to work on real investment projects, market research, portfolio strategy, and finance-related events as a team. The club is open to all majors and experience levels. Whether your interest is investing, finance careers, or simply building practical skills alongside motivated peers, the Investment Club provides a space to contribute, collaborate, and grow through shared projects rather than passive instruction. Monday meetings are for people who miss Friday or people who want help with the investment contest.
regularMeetingLocation: Mondays cob 1 room 276 3-4 and Fridays cob 2 140 4:30-6:30

name: iSight: Pre-Optometry & Vision
description: A social, yet professional community where aspiring optometrists can learn and thrive together. With the ultimate end goal of advancing and succeeding in optometry school, the necessary tools provided through the organization include shadowing and internship opportunities, easy connections to local optometrists and students, as well as gaining optic and graduate school knowledge.

name: JOYS
description: The mission of JOYS (Just Offering You Smiles) is to bring joy, encouragement, and hope to youth in the foster care system. Through care packages, supplies, handwritten letters and meaningful connections, we aim to remind everybody that they are seen, valued, and loved. JOYS is dedicated to supporting foster youth with kindness, consistency, and care, while also fostering a culture of service and leadership among UC Merced students.

name: Kairos
description: Kairos is an API organization devoted to providing a safe community space for the Asian and Pacific Islander population on campus! Kairos is made up of four main sectors: dance, social, cultural, and tech crew. Our dance sector is noncompetitive; Kairos focuses on having fun and teaching engaging dances that represent API cultures from modern and traditional perspectives. Our social sector holds general meetings biweekly to get together and build a community! Our cultural sector also holds general meetings biweekly. These meetings involve discussions that dive into what it means to be a minority in America, as well as the cultures we interact with in order to gain a better understanding of ourselves and the world around us. Lastly, Tech Crew works on photography, filming, post production, and our instagram posts!

name: Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc.
description: Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc. is a historically African American fraternity. Since the fraternity's founding on January 5, 1911, at Indiana University Bloomington, it has never restricted membership based on color, creed, or national origin, though membership traditionally is dominated by black men. The Pi Beta Chapter, chartered on March 25, 2006, at California State University, Fresno, and extending its brotherhood to the University of California, Merced, is dedicated to developing men of character who are committed to making a meaningful impact in their communities and beyond. Through scholarship, fellowship, and civic engagement, our members strive to uphold the Fraternity's founding mission of guiding men along the lines of social, intellectual, and moral achievement.

name: Kappa Delta Chi
description: "The Purpose of Kappa Delta Chi is to promote the values of Unity, Honesty, Integrity and Leadership among women at colleges and universities. Through numerous service events, sisterhood retreats, and academic and cultural workshops, KDChis learn more about themselves, each other and their surrounding Universities and communities. They blossom into committed leaders, are able to network with our remarkable alumnae, and continue to serve as civic leaders well past their graduation. KDChi is a non-traditional sorority full of diverse members and eager women ready to make a difference in our communities. With sisters, anything is possible." - Kappa Delta Chi Sorority Inc.

name: Kappa Kappa Gamma
description: Kappa Kappa Gamma is an organization of women, which seeks for every member throughout her life bonds of friendship, mutual support, opportunities for self-growth, respect for intellectual development, and an understanding of and an allegiance to positive ethical principles. We’re a women’s organization. It starts with that. But where we go from there is up to the woman. Kappa Kappa Gamma offers a member experience ranging from friendship to mentoring, from leadership to service and from campus activities to a lifetime of community involvement.

name: Korean Student Association
description: The Korean Student Association (KSA) at UC Merced is dedicated to empowering Korean, Korean-American, and international Korean students through identity-centered support, mentorship, and leadership development. Rather than focusing solely on cultural celebration, KSA prioritizes helping students feel at home, academically, socially, and emotionally, within the UC Merced community. Through our Gajok Program (GP) and peer-based initiatives, we foster a close-knit network where students can connect over shared experiences, build confidence, and grow into leaders rooted in cultural pride and personal belonging. While our mission centers on the lived experiences of Korean-identifying students, we welcome anyone with an interest in Korean culture to join and be part of our growing community.

name: La Familia
description: Our three pillars, Academic Scholarship, Community Service, and Social Interaction, lay the foundation for La Familia. It is the primary objective of an Academic Scholarship for Familia members to pursue an education at an institution of higher learning. Taking part in community service represents an Hermano's commitment to better the surrounding community. The goal of Social Interaction is to ease the transition to an institution for incoming Familia members while providing opportunities for networking for future success. Developing partnerships and alliances necessary to fulfill La Familia's mission is achieved through the fulfillment of the three pillars. All three pillars should be approached with an equal amount of concern, time, and intensity. (La Familia Constitution) Mission Statement: The Mission of La Familia is to cultivate an environment of inclusion, professional development, and hermandad. We aim to raise the retention rate of self-identifying Latinos in the pursuit of higher education through the integration of the concept of La Nueva Persona and the use of three pillars: Academic Scholarship, Community Service, and Social InteractionVision: La Nueva Persona

name: Lambda Alliance
description: Lambda Alliance provides a safe and inclusive space for all individuals to self-express and discuss identity and LGBTQ+ issues. As a registered club and organization, we celebrate the intersectionality of various identities. We strengthen and support the community by hosting social events and learning opportunities.
