We also create an opportunity for allies to educate themselves and advocate alongside the LGBTQ+ community. We recognize that individuals are at different phases in developing their identities and hope to support them in their journey. In doing so, we advocate for the protection of, the rights of, and respect for the LGBTQ+ community.

name: Mandarin & Cantonese Language Exchange
description: Mandarin & Cantonese Language Exchange is a student organization mainly focused on practical language exchange, peer learning, and communication. Through conversation practice, language partner activities, and interactive events, members can develop Mandarin and Cantonese skills in an informal and supportive environment.The organization also highlights the linguistic diversity of Chinese-speaking communities, especially the relationship between Mandarin and Cantonese. MCLE welcomes learners, heritage speakers, and native speakers who are interested in language exchange and cross-cultural communication.

name: Margo F. Souza Student Leadership Center
description: The Margo F. Souza Student Leadership Center aspires to develop students' leadership skills, knowledge, capacity, and self-efficacy while also empowering students to thrive as life-long learners and leaders in the 21st century. The Souza Leadership Center is a unit within The Office of Leadership, Service and Career. The center would not exist without the generous contributions of Central Valley local Margo F. Souza, a champion for student leadership at UC Merced.

name: Mariachi los Bobcats
description: Mariachi Los Bobcats de UC MercedMariachi Los Bobcats is UC Merced’s student-led mariachi ensemble, dedicated to celebrating, performing, and sharing the rich musical traditions of mariachi and regional Mexican music with the campus and surrounding community.Our organization brings students together through music, performance, cultural appreciation, and community. We strive to create a welcoming environment where members can develop their skills as musicians and performers, learn from one another, and contribute to an ensemble built on collaboration, commitment, and respect for the traditions we represent.Mariachi Los Bobcats welcomes students with a wide range of musical backgrounds. Whether someone has years of mariachi experience, comes from another musical tradition, or is interested in developing new skills, we believe that dedication and a willingness to learn are essential parts of building a strong ensemble.Through rehearsals, campus events, community performances, and collaborations with other organizations, we aim to promote greater appreciation for mariachi music while contributing to the cultural and artistic life of UC Merced.Above all, Mariachi Los Bobcats is a community. We seek to create a space where students can make music together, build lasting connections, grow as performers, and proudly carry mariachi forward for future generations of Bobcats.

name: Martial Arts Club
description: We are the "Martial Arts Club at University of California, Merced."We are a social and cultural club that aims to teach and practice various styles of martial arts; spread interest and understanding in the martial arts; and develop self-discipline and confidence in our students.We strive to bridge the gap between the local Merced community and UC Merced.And most importantly, we have fun as a club and help contribute to the campus culture at UC Merced for current and future students.

name: Materials Research Society
description: The Materials Research Society chapter aims to build a dynamic and interactive interdisciplinary community of student and faculty researchers to improve the understanding of materials while promoting a social and intellectual environment.

name: Math Club at UC Merced
description: At The Math Club, our primary objective is to create an environment where mathematical ideas can flourish, and minds can thrive, arousing and maintaining interest in mathematics. We seek to inspire a deep appreciation for the subject while nurturing a strong sense of camaraderie among our members. Through a range of interactive activities, discussions, and problem-solving sessions, we aim to make mathematics accessible, enjoyable, and relevant to all.

name: MEDLIFE
description: MEDLIFE is a volunteer-led global health organization with a mission to help families achieve greater freedom from the constraints of poverty, empowering them to live healthier lives. We seek to achieve this goal by partnering with motivated individuals from communities experiencing poverty and working to improve their access to Medicine, Education, and Community Development. Along with affiliate Chapters, MEDLIFE at UC Merced raises money for Medicine, Education, and Community Development projects for low-income families around the world. We are committed to learning about the inequalities of global issues while promoting MEDLIFE's mission within our local community.

name: Merced 4 K-pop
description: The fundamental goal of M4k is to focus on K-pop dances presented by esteemed Korean groups, including but not limited to Itzy, NewJeans, and Aespa, as well as prominent boy groups such as BTS, Ateez, NCT, and others. Our club is dedicated to a collaborative learning experience, facilitated through workshops organized by M4k, unit practices, and concerted efforts to recapture the intrinsic essence of the original choreography. The inclusive atmosphere of the club emphasizes mutual support, fostering a sense of camaraderie as we embark on this journey together.

name: Merced Badminton Club
description: The UC Merced Badminton Club aims to provide a place for students who play badminton to connect with each other. We welcome anyone with an interest in badminton, no matter if you are a complete beginner or have many years of experience. We strongly believe in making resources on how and where students can play badminton in Merced accessible to all who may be looking for them.For information regarding events, please join our discord server and our instagram to stay updated: Discord - https://discord.gg/wuEwrSQKInstagram - @mercedbadmintonclubIf you have any questions, please feel free to email us at: badmntn.club.ucm@gmail.com

name: Merced Cybersecurity
description: Merced Cybersecurity is a cybersecurity club at UC Merced, dedicated to empowering students with the skills and knowledge needed to navigate the ever-evolving world of cybersecurity. Whether you're a beginner or an experienced hacker, our club provides hands-on learning experiences to develop your technical expertise.We specialize in:🔹 Cybersecurity Education – Learn about ethical hacking, network security, cryptography, and digital forensics through interactive lessons and workshops.🔹 Capture The Flag (CTF) Competitions – Sharpen your problem-solving skills by competing in cybersecurity challenges against teams from across the world.🔹 Workshops & Training – Gain real-world experience with tools and techniques used by professionals in the field.🔹 Collegiate Cyber Defense Competition (CCDC) – Put your defensive skills to the test by protecting networks against simulated cyberattacks.If you're interested in learning more, please join our discord  https://discord.gg/XUTut3GN7AJoin UC Merced Cyber to explore the exciting world of cybersecurity, enhance your technical skills, and connect with a community of like-minded individuals passionate about security and ethical hacking! Merced Cybersecurity ranked #13 out of 39 teams at the most  Western Region CCDC 2025 Qualifers.

name: Merced Indian Graduate Student Association
description: Merced Indian Graduate Student Association (MIGSA) is an organization founded with the purpose dedicated to the cultural development of Indian Graduate students at UC Merced. MIGSA primarily consists of graduate students and postdoctoral scholars. Through the various events hosted, MIGSA creates a platform for graduate students to connect, celebrate and appreciate Indian culture. MIGSA also actively assists incoming students by guiding them in every way possible.

name: Merced Pokémon
description: We are a Pokémon club that mainly plays Pokémon go but we encompass every Pokémon game and Anime. We host official Pokémon go meetups that are community oriented. Playing the game encourages mobility and interactions, which will benefit their physical, and mental health. We hope to support serious semi and pro players in any Pokémon game.Discord serverhttps://discord.gg/MEkS3s53tG

name: Merced Pre-Law Society
description: The Merced Pre-Law Society has a mission to get students to law school. As a club, we are not only here for students who are well on their way to law school but are also a club for students to explore the legal field to see if it is something they are interested in. Our goal is to be able to give our members the resources necessary to help them get into and be successful in law school. Our club will be collaborating with different clubs on campus and putting on a variety of events available to UC Merced students. Our events will include but are not limited to having guest speakers, giving law school information, LSAT prep questions, admission sessions, law school visits, Moot court, and legal internships. We strive to be a way for students to work on professional development not only for law school but the work field as well. MPLS meetings are Tuesdays from 6:30 - 7:30pm in COB2 266 for the Fall 2026 semester. Follow our instagram @ucm.mpls for updates as well!Contact MPLS President Michelle Thomas at michellethomas@ucmerced.edu for more information!

name: Mi3 Student Association
description: The Mi3 Student Association at UC Merced, short for Machine Intelligence, Interaction, and Imagination, is a dedicated community of students passionate about machine learning, computer vision and their applications within autonomous systems. Our mission is to advance research within this field and to provide opportunities for students to learn about cutting-edge research, gain hands-on experience with real-world applications,engage with academic and industry professionals at major conferences, workshops, and networking events, and build a social community for UC Merced students passionate about machine intelligence. Whether you're an experienced researcher or just beginning your journey in AI, our organization welcomes all who share a curiosity for the future of machine intelligence.

name: Middle Ground
description: “The purpose(s) of this organization shall be to bridge the gap between 2 different ends of politics, hence Democrats and Republicans to create compromise and civil discussions about politics. The intended impact of the organization on the University is to educate young people on the role of politics in their lives and to build into a community of civil conversations on a range of issues in our lives. The services provided are social bonding, understanding the complexity of politics, and how world/domestic issues/events affect our life as everyday citizens.”

name: Minecraft Club at UC Merced
description: Minecraft Club at UC Merced is a student organization focused on bringing together students and members of the UC Merced community through Minecraft, gaming, creativity, and collaborative projects. The club provides a welcoming space for members to socialize, participate in Minecraft events, competitions, survival activities, collaborative builds, and community projects, and contribute to the development and improvement of the club’s Minecraft server.Members may participate in a variety of areas depending on their interests, including building, game design, coding and plugin development, art and texture creation, event planning, server moderation, and general gameplay. The organization is designed to combine both social and technical aspects of Minecraft, allowing members from different majors and skill levels to work together on shared projects while also providing a casual community for students to meet others and have fun.No prior technical experience or advanced Minecraft knowledge is required to participate. Whether you enjoy building, programming, exploring, competing, creating, or simply playing with others, the Minecraft Club at UC Merced aims to provide a place for you to get involved.

name: Mission:BRAIN Chapter at UC Merced
description: Mission:BRAIN at the University of California, Merced is dedicated to expanding educational and professional opportunities for students interested in neurosurgery, neurology, and neuroscience research. Our chapter is strongly committed to addressing global healthcare disparities. Through seminars, mentorship programs, and research experiences, we connect students with medical professionals to enrich their education and career readiness. By engaging in community outreach and advocacy, we focus on empowering the Central California region, raising awareness of neurological conditions, and promoting improved access to neurosurgical care in medically underserved areas.

name: Model Shipbuilding Club
description: The purpose of the MSC is to:Provide students with hands-on experience in model shipbuilding, including 3D printing, electrical engineering, and RC conversion.Foster interdisciplinary collaboration among students interested in engineering, art, history, and hands-on projects.Promote community engagement through activities such as programs for children, donating repurposed models, and fundraising for local museums and community centers.Encourage interest in maritime history, naval engineering, and scale modeling through field trips, guest speakers, and competitions.

name: Movimiento Estudiantil Chicano de Aztlán
description: El Movimiento Estudiantil Chicano de Aztlán, also known as "MEChA", is a student organization that promotes advocacy for marginalized communities while creating a safe space for social, political, and cultural ideas/opinions. Our organization strives to educate the Merced community on the importance of maintaining the longevity of La Causa while creating a strong sense of unity to defeat the stigma of Latinx stereotypes. This organization was built on a Chicano-based movement which has now been developed to help amplify the voices of all marginalized communities.

name: Multicultural Medical Alliance
description: The Multicultural Medical Alliance at UC Merced, establish this organization to provide accessible health education, community service, outreach, and advocacy to underserved and underrepresented communities. Through volunteerism, educational initiatives, and community engagement, MMA strives to promote physical, mental, and emotional well-being while encouraging cultural inclusivity and compassion within healthcare spaces.The organization is committed to empowering individuals through preventative health education, inspiring future healthcare professionals, and creating meaningful opportunities for students to serve their communities through leadership, outreach, and service.

name: Muslim Students Association
description: We, the Muslim students of University of California, Merced, out of our faith and dedication to the service of Islam, do hereby proclaim the establishment of the Muslim Students Association, so that collectively we can share in a common set of moral commitments rooted in the message of Islam; engage in religious, social and community activities; support educational and intellectual pursuits; and continue to promote the goals of Muslim students in University of California, Merced, and thus serve our faith as best we can.

name: My Little Pony Club
description: My Little Pony Club at UC Merced is a welcoming community for My Little Pony enthusiasts, fans, and anyone interested in connecting with others who share an appreciation for the series and its characters.Our goal is to create a safe and inclusive space where members can be themselves, meet fellow fans, build friendships, and share their interests. Through social gatherings, discussions, creative activities, entertainment, and other events, we hope to provide opportunities for members to connect both around My Little Pony and beyond.Whether you have been a fan for years, recently discovered the series, or simply want to meet people with similar interests, everyone is welcome. My Little Pony Club is a place to celebrate the community, creativity, friendship, and joy that My Little Pony brings to its fans.

name: National Alliance on Mental Illness
description: NAMI on Campus is a student-led organization that focuses on promoting mental health awareness, advocacy, and support within a college or university community. The club typically hosts events, workshops, and activities to educate students about mental health, reduce stigma, and provide peer support. It may also connect members to local mental health resources and create a safe space for discussions about mental well-being.

name: National Society of Black Engineers
description: On behalf of the National Society of Black Engineers (NSBE) at the University of California, Merced, we would like to cordially welcome you to build a partnership and join the largest student-managed organization in the world. NSBE is a non-profit organization whose mission is to "increase the number of culturally responsible Black engineers who excel academically, succeed professionally, and positively impact the community." NSBE transforms young minority students into leaders and professionals who can positively and effectively function in the corporate and professional world. At the University of California, Merced we have not only had success in living out our mission, but also in the recruitment, retention, and graduation of qualified minorities in the STEM fields. Our chapter programmatic efforts target retention, academic excellence, leadership development, and civic engagement. Every year we seek to expand and enhance our goals. Please join us in living the mission and you will be able to benefit from all that NSBE has to offer. Contact any Executive Board Member for more information!If you have any questions please email: nsbe@ucmerced.edu

name: Native and Indigenous Student Coalition
description: The organization is exclusively for charitable, educational, and cultural purposes. As an organization, we strive to provide better communication among Native and Indigenous students, Native communities, the University community, and the broader public. Within the organization, we plan to develop student-initiated and student-run outreach and retention projects geared toward the success of Native people achieving higher education.

name: Nigerian Student Association
description: The Nigerian Students Association (NSA) at UC Merced is dedicated to fostering and promoting Nigerian culture and heritage within our campus community. Our primary goal is to provide a platform where students can learn about and celebrate the rich traditions and history of Nigeria. We aim to bring awareness to the Nigerian American diaspora, both in California and across the nation, highlighting the contributions and experiences of Nigerians everywhere.In addition to cultural education, NSA is committed to creating a space for positive social interactions and unity among Nigerian students at UC Merced. We organize events and activities that encourage dialogue, collaboration, and mutual understanding. By embracing and celebrating our diverse backgrounds and perspectives, we embody the beauty and strength found in our collective differences.Join us as we explore the vibrant beauty of the Nigerian culture, connect with one another, and build a supportive community at UC Merced.

name: Nikkei Student Union
description: Konnichiwa!Nikkei Student Union is a Japanese American association on campus! Anyone is welcome to join us in learning more Japanese culture and doing some activities like calligraphy, origami, etc. We also help those who are looking into studying abroad or internships in Japan! ?For more info about Nikkei Student Union, please contact: agutierrez291@ucmerced.eduWe also have a Taiko committee called Yamabuki Taiko! Taiko is a traditional Japanese drum and they are so stress relieving! We have practice every week and anyone is welcome to come watch our practices. Maybe you could try it out too!If you're interested in finding out more on Yamabuki Taiko:?Instagram: Follow us on our Instagram for the latest information and events!Interest Form: Interested in being contacted for practice and other updates? Please fill out the interest form here!Email: Please contact with any questions: achan127@ucmerced.edu

name: Nintendo Wii Club
description: Wanna chillax with your fellow Bobcats while playing some classic Wii games? Then this is the club for you! Join today to sit back and play some of the more than 5,000 games available on the Wii! The most important rule is to have fun!

name: NOBCChE (National Organization for the Professional Advancement of Black Chemists and Chemical Engineers)UC Merced Chapter
description: The UC Merced Chapter of National Organization for the Professional Advancement of Black Chemists and Chemical Engineers (NOBCChE)  is an inclusive, intellectually vibrant community that advances the academic, professional, and leadership development of undergraduate and graduate students in chemistry, chemical engineering, and related disciplines.The purpose of this organization is:•    To promote scientific engagement: Foster interest in chemistry, chemical engineering, and related STEM fields among students through workshops, seminars, and hands-on experiences.•  To encourage research and innovation: Support undergraduate and graduate research by providing opportunities to explore new methods, techniques, and discoveries in chemistry and related disciplines.•    To facilitate networking and knowledge exchange: Create spaces for students to exchange ideas, collaborate on projects, and connect with professionals, alumni, and faculty in chemical sciences and related fields.•    To champion diversity, inclusion and representation: Advance the mission of NOBCChE by advocating for the representation and success of Black scientists and engineers within the academic, research, and professional communities.•   To promote professional development: Prepare students for successful careers by offering mentorship, resume building, professional development, and leadership opportunities in STEM.

name: Off Duty Wellness
description: Off Duty Wellness is a women-centered wellness and lifestyle organization dedicated to creating a supportive community focused on movement, confidence, connection, and personal growth. Our goal is to provide members with opportunities to prioritize their physical and mental well-being while building meaningful friendships and lasting memories.Through a variety of wellness and social experiences, members can participate in Pilates classes, yoga sessions, tennis court practices, group workouts, running clubs, wellness walks, hiking adventures, and outdoor fitness activities. Off Duty Wellness also hosts team dinners, celebrations, self-care events, workshops, and community gatherings that encourage connection and a balanced lifestyle.Our organization welcomes students of all fitness levels and backgrounds who are interested in wellness, personal development, and being part of a positive and empowering community. Off Duty Wellness aims to inspire members to build healthy habits, grow in confidence, and enjoy a lifestyle centered around wellness, friendship, and fun.ODW stands for Owning your wellness, Discovering your strength, and Welcoming positive change into your life while being off duty from the stress of academics, work, social pressures, and everyday responsibilities. Through movement, connection, and community, we empower members to recharge, grow, and thrive both on and off campus.

name: Office of Financial Aid & Scholarships
description: The Office of Financial Aid & Scholarships is committed to the success of our students by providing financial aid and advising services that support student recruitment, retention, and timely degree completion, and ensures that a world-class education remains within reach for all eligible students who need financial assistance to achieve their educational goals.

name: Office of Social Justice Initiatives and Identity Programs
description: The Office of Social Justice Initiatives & Identity Programs (SJI&IP) at UC Merced is dedicated to ensuring every scholar thrives in our multicultural and global society. The Office of Social Justice Initiatives & Identity Programs is committed to transforming UC Merced into a space where historically underserved scholars not only stay, but thrive. Through intentional programming, intersectional community building, and unapologetic student empowerment, we foster belonging, justice, and liberation for all.We are committed to advocating for and serving UC Merced’s diverse scholar community, actively influencing university policies and practices to establish our campus as a hub for transformative leadership and social change.

name: Office of Student Involvement
description: The staff of the Office of Student Involvement looks forward to helping you to achieve your personal, academic, and career goals. Getting involved on campus will enable you to amplify your voice, develop your leadership skills and connect with the diverse and inclusive environment on campus. Those who are actively engaged both inside and outside of the classroom are more likely to stay in college through graduation. Engagement on campus is the most significant predictor of persistence. The Office of Student Involvement oversees Registered Clubs and Organizations (RCO), Fraternity & Sorority Life (FSL), Associated Students of University of California, Merced (ASUCM), ASUCM Campus Activites Board (CAB), Business Center, and the Law Clinic.MISSION STATEMENT:The Office of Student Involvement is committed to building a sense of belonging and school spirit by helping students explore ways to get involved on campus, develop new leadership skills, and engage in meaningful experiences that will prepare them for the opportunities of tomorrow. OSI is here to help encourage involvement in campus life, support student initiatives, and serve as the primary liaison for student organizations. Invest in your own success, get involved in over 240+ clubs and organizations!

name: Office of Student Rights and Responsibilities
description: The Office of Student Rights and Responsibilities at UC Merced supports student success through services designed to promote integrity, ethical decision making, effective communication, and conflict management in alignment with the Principles of Community. In addition to administering the Code of Student Conduct including the academic integrity process, our services center around student advocacy and agency. We teach students the skills necessary to engage in learning that encourages personal accountability, develops resilience and fosters a community of care.
regularMeetingTime: In-Person Services Available: Weekdays, 9 AM - 5 PM

name: Office of the Ombuds
description: The Office of the Ombuds is a safe confidential and informal place where UC Merced community members can go for informal assistance with managing conflict, complaints, and concerns with a colleague, classmate, supervisor or anyone else on campus. The Ombuds will listen; help identify options; make inquiries and make referrals as appropriate; and/or facilitate resolutions in an impartial manner.

name: Operation Smile Club
description: Our club is on a mission to make healthcare accessible to every child in the world, regardless of their background or where they live. We believe that every child deserves the chance to live a healthy and fulfilling life, and we’re committed to making that a reality. By providing support to children born with cleft lips in developing countries, we’re taking the first step towards creating a world where no child is left behind. We’re also dedicated to raising awareness about the lack of access to healthcare around the world, and we’re working tirelessly to make a difference. Join us in our fight for a better future, and let's make a positive impact together.

name: Paleontology and Life
description: Established in January 2023, the Paleontology and Life Organization (PAL) at University of California, Merced is dedicated to providing students with hands-on experiences in the natural sciences beyond the traditional classroom. Through programs focused on paleontology, wildlife conservation, zoology, museum and natural sciences, PAL helps students develop skills and connections within the community.In partnership with the Fossil Discovery Center of Madera County, members gain experience in fossil preservation, specimen preparation, museum outreach, and educational programming. PAL also collaborates with Stanislaus Wildlife Care Center and Applegate Park Zoo to provide students with opportunities in wildlife rehabilitation, animal care, zoological husbandry, conservation education, and hands-on work with live animals.To Understand Our Past, Is to Protect Our Future.

name: Panjabi Students' Union
description: Panjabi Students' Union is an organization for ALL students, with the focus on academic support and preserving the culture of the Punjabi ethenic group. Join the club to be provided with Academic Resources, mentorship, peer support, and much more to help you succeed in your academic journey. The Panjabi Students' Union is also a great space to learn about the Punjabi Culture, language, traditions, and values. Members will also experience the spirit of Punjabi hospitality.Our purpose is to create an environment where students can grow academically and personally, while also engaging in cultural events, discussions, and activities. It does not matter if you are Punjabi or simply interested in learning more; We welcome you to be part of a diverse community that fosters academic success, cultural appreciation, and lifelong connections.

name: PERIOD. at UC Merced
description: PERIOD. at UC Merced is a student-led organization dedicated to fighting period poverty and breaking the stigma surrounding menstruation. We believe that access to menstrual products is a basic human right, yet many individuals- whether due to financial barriers, homelessness, incarceration, or cultural stigma- struggle to obtain them.Our chapter works to address this issue through product donation drives, menstrual product packing parties, educational workshops on reproductive and menstrual health, and community outreach. We also aim to create safe spaces for conversation, advocacy, and awareness on campus, while providing meaningful volunteer opportunities that connect UC Merced students with the wider Merced community.By joining PERIOD. at UC Merced, students become part of a movement for menstrual equity and social change, building leadership skills while making a tangible impact in the lives of others.

name: Phi Mu
description: Phi Mu was founded in 1852, making it the second oldest sisterhood. Three young women came together to form a Philomathean Society which was later renamed Phi Mu. Being the second oldest sisterhood, it has allowed us to grow our individual chapters all around the nation as well as create such a strong bond as one united sisterhood. The Children’s Miracle Network Hospital has been Phi Mu’s primary philanthropy since 1986. Since its official adoption as the only philanthropy in 1994, colligate and alumnae have raised more than 21 million dollars to date for more than 170 hospitals nationwide.With more than 230,000 initiated members, 137 colligate chapters and, 145 alumnae chapters, Phi Mu will always be there for you when you need it most. You can always count on a Phi Mu sister to be right by your side through the lightest and darkest times of life. At Phi Mu, we promote vibrant living, encouraging members to achieve their personal best with the support of their sisters.On April 16th, 2016, the Eta Sigma chapter was initiated and installed as the 130th chapter of Phi Mu Fraternity.

name: Pi Kappa Phi
description: Pi Kappa Phi is a social fraternity founded on December 10th, 1904. Rushing Pi Kappa Phi promises to be a life-changing experience. You will build friendships and relationships that will last a lifetime. You will develop leadership and communication skills. You will also receive career and academic advice from experienced members and alumni and job connections for the future.Our brotherhood actively lives up to our 7 core values:Common LoyaltyAccountabilityPersonal ResponsibilityCampus InvolvementAchievement Responsible CitizenshipLifelong CommitmentPi Kappa Phi also operates its own philanthropy, The Ability Experience (formerly known as Push America), which works with individual chapters to serve people with disabilities.

name: Pilipinx American Alliance
description: In the ongoing attempt to serve and interact with the Pilipinx/Filipinx/Filipinx-American community, the Pilipinx-American Alliance stands to promote a network of social support through the encouragement of political struggle, academic excellence, and cultural awareness while celebrating cultural diversity.

name: Pre-Veterinary Club
description: The Pre-Veterinary club at the University of California Merced aims to guide students of all years and all backgrounds in the field of Veterinary Medicine by providing activities that enhance their preparation for veterinary school. We strive to offer as many resources at UC Merced for students from underrepresented/disadvantaged communities by providing a broader perspective on veterinary medicine to freshmen and sophomores and support to juniors and seniors that are in the application process. Our meetings include presentations from Admission Officers at prospective veterinary schools; Veterinarians who quiz students on animal care; and a chance to make a difference in our community through volunteer work. Members have a chance to voice their opinions, aid in planning potential field trips, start fundraisers, practice public speaking, be a part of officer meetings, and the opportunity to create an impact on campus. For more information or interest in joining, please email pvc.ucmerced@gmail.com

name: Professional Fraternity Council
description: The Professional Fraternity Council, also referred to as PFC,  promotes and enhances professional fraternities on campus by serving as a cooperative forum for sharing ideas, information, experiences, and concerns while increasing the awareness of professional fraternities on campus.  PFC exists to stimulate interaction among its member groups, creating a spirit of fellowship among students.Business Fraternities: Alpha Kappa PsiDelta Sigma PiEngineering Fraternities:Theta TauPre-Health FraternitiesDelta Epsilon MuCurrently Inactive: Service FraternitiesAlpha Phi Omega﻿Pre-Law Fraternities Phi Alpha DeltaPre-Medicine FraternitiesPhi Delta Epsilon﻿

name: Project Rural India Social and Health Improvement
description: Project RISHI (Rural India Social and Health Improvement) at UC Merced is a student-led organization focused on supporting sustainable development and improving health and well being in rural communities in India. As a chapter of Project RISHI, we work with communities to support long term projects related to public health, health education, sanitation, nutrition, environmental sustainability, and community development. Our chapter brings together UC Merced students who are interested in public health, global health, service, and making a difference in underserved communities. Members can get involved through fundraising, campus events, educational activities, and community based projects while also learning more about the social and health challenges that different communities face. We also hope to build a community at UC Merced where students can meet others with similar interests, gain leadership experience, and become more involved in global health and service. Ultimately, our goal is to create a lasting Project RISHI chapter at UC Merced that continues to grow and make a meaningful impact both on campus and beyond.

name: Project Smile: Pre-Dental Society
description: Project Smile is a pre-dental student organization at UC Merced dedicated to education, service, and professional development. Through hands-on activities, dental school visits, volunteering, and community outreach, we provide students with opportunities to explore dentistry while promoting oral health and giving back to our community.

name: Project Women  and Youth
description: Project W.A.Y (Women and Youth) is a student-led organization at UC Merced dedicated to empowering the health of underserved populations, with a focus on women and children. We will provide oppurtunities through health advocacy, mentorship, and community service, we work to improve health outcomes and eliminate barriers to accessing essential healthcare. Our members participate in volunteer opportunities, community service projects, personal initiatives, and more oppurtunities. All UC Merced students are welcome to join!

name: Psi Chi: The International Honor Society in Psychology
description: Psi Chi is the International Honor Society of Psychology for undergraduate psychology students, founded in 1929. The UC Merced chapter of Psi Chi was started in 2011 and was one of the college's first honor societies. Since its inception, our chapter's goals have been to help psychology students network with their peers and professors, take advantage of research and career opportunities, and attend psychology-related events and workshops.The chapter works to nourish and stimulate professional growth through programs designed to augment and enhance the regular curriculum and to provide practical experience and fellowship through affiliation with the chapter.If you have any questions regarding our club, any suggestions about what you would like, or are interested in becoming involved as a member or an officer, please feel free to contact gmorgan4@ucmerced.edu at any time!

name: Psychology Club
description: Welcome to Psychology Club! We are so glad that you are interested in our club!The Psychology Club works alongside Psi Chi, an honors psychology organization. We provide an opportunity for psychology undergraduates and other students interested in psychology to explore new topics that they would not learn about in the classroom and provide them with opportunities and resources that will enhance their academic careers. We will help our members prepare for graduate school, provide opportunities for volunteer work, and work to provide our members with potential research opportunities. If you have any questions regarding our club, any suggestions about what you would like, or are interested in becoming involved as a member or an officer, please feel free to contact gmorgan4@ucmerced.edu at any time!

name: Public Health Graduate Student Group
description: The Public Health Graduate Student Group aims to create a healthy collaboration, a positive experience, and effective communication among PH graduate students, faculty and staff. We also aim to provide academic (e.g., writing groups, stats workshops, etc.), professional (e.g., post-grad life tips, time management, CV/Resume workshops, etc.), and social events (e.g., game night, crafts, etc.).

name: Public Health Society
description: Public Health Society (PHS) is a team of students at UC Merced growing and working together to open doors of opportunities for each other to learn about the diverse options that the Public Health field has to offer; as well as the impact that it can have on the community. Through our three pillars -- Prevent, Promote, Protect -- the members of Public Health Society will engage with both the local community, as well as abroad, to share our knowledge and practice of what we learn. All majors welcome!

name: RadioBio
description: RadioBio is a podcast where UC Merced biology graduate students talk with scientists about biological systems, from molecules to ecosystems.

name: Raunak Merced Di
description: “The purpose of this organization shall be to serve as a hub for the Punjabi students and other interested students of the academic community here at UC Merced to interact, dance, and share experiences of the Punjabi culture as well as give its members the opportunity to represent the Punjabi culture to the greater community in the city of Merced as well as the university”

name: Research and Development
description: The UC Merced Research and Development (RnD) Club is a collaborative, project-driven organization where students explore emerging technologies across machine learning, software engineering, embedded systems, and interdisciplinary engineering fields. Our mission is to create a hands-on environment that bridges academic learning with real-world research and development practices. RnD focuses on building a strong community of students who are passionate about designing, developing, and iterating on real technical projects. Members work in teams to take ideas from concept to implementation, simulating real industry and research workflows. Through this process, students gain experience in brainstorming, prototyping, testing, and refining solutions while learning to collaborate effectively in technical teams.By participating in the club, members develop practical skills in areas such as machine learning, data analysis, software development, systems design, and project management. In addition, students gain exposure to tools and workflows used in industry and research environments, helping them build strong technical foundations and a portfolio of meaningful, real-world projects. Our goal is to foster a community of builders and researchers who are not only consumers of technology, but active creators contributing innovative solutions to real problems.

name: Robotics Society
description: The Robotics Society at UC Merced is a student-run organization focused on hands-on engineering, robotics design, and interdisciplinary technical projects. Our goal is to provide students with practical experience in robotics, automation, electronics, and mechanical design through collaborative projects, workshops, and competitions.The club is open to students of all experience levels and backgrounds, ranging from beginners interested in learning fundamentals to advanced members working on complex systems. Projects may include competitive robotics, autonomous systems, mechatronics, and applied engineering builds.The Robotics Society also aims to foster collaboration with other engineering and STEM organizations on campus, promote professional development, and create an inclusive environment where students can learn, build, and grow together.
regularMeetingTime: Every Tuesday 7-9pm (Subject to change! Check Discord announcements)

name: Rock Band Club
description: The members of Rock Band Club, who share deep enthusiasm for rock culture, are dedicated to creating a supportive environment that nurtures community engagement, artistic growth, and musical collaboration. We strive to maintain respect and inclusivity within the community while fostering the creativity that comes with rock music's long-standing community!

name: Rotaract Club
description: Established in 2006, the Rotaract Club at UC Merced provides an opportunity for young men and women to enhance the knowledge and skills that will assist them in personal development, to address the physical and social needs of their community, and to promote better relations between all people worldwide through a framework of friendship and service.

name: SAE International
description: Welcome to the SAE International (formerly Society of Automotive Engineers) chapter (a.k.a. Bobcat Racing EV) at UC Merced, a project-based organization dedicated to advancing sustainable mobility. Our club is at the forefront of engineering innovation, where we design, build, and race electric vehicles that prioritize eco-friendly transportation solutions. Through hands-on projects, we foster an environment that empowers members to contribute to a cleaner and more efficient automotive industry. Join us as we drive progress and create a lasting impact on the future of sustainable transportation.

name: Sigma Chi
description: "One, and the main, aim and object of Sigma Chi has been, and is, to develop and train broad-minded men who can recognize the wholeness of things and who are not bound down to a contracted, eight-by-ten notion of exclusiveness."— Benjamin Piatt Runkle, FounderSigma Chi is a brotherhood built on values, leadership, and showing up for each other. At UC Merced, we push each other to grow, not just as students, but as men. Our goal is to build something real, where accountability, respect, and lifelong friendships actually mean something.We’re one of the most active fraternities on campus in terms of philanthropy, events, and community service. From raising the most philanthropic money for the Huntsman Cancer Institute to leading student orgs and showing out at campus events.If you’re looking for something deeper than just letters, a place where leaders of men have your back and you’re pushed to be better, Sigma Chi is that.

name: Sigma Delta Pi
description: Sigma Delta Pi, the National Collegiate Hispanic Honor Society is a non-profit organization whose purpose is to honor those who attain excellence in the study of the Spanish language. In the study of the literature and culture of the Spanish-speaking peoples, we honor those who have made the Hispanic contributions to modern culture in order to encourage college and university students to acquire a greater interest in and a deeper understanding of Hispanic culture. Sigma Delta Pi fosters friendly relations and mutual respect between the nations of Hispanic speech and those of English speech, and serves its membership in ways which will contribute to the attainment of the goals and ideals of the society.

name: Sigma Theta Psi
description: Sigma Theta Psi is an academic and social Sorority & Fraternity with a purpose to form relationships amongst a group of individuals who will carry on a lifetime of friendships with each other. We are a unity of individuals that recognize the trials students face, and are dedicated to assisting them through their educational and life endeavors.The founding mothers of Sigma Theta Psi created the sorority on November 13, 1991 at San Jose State University to fill a void of multicultural awareness on their campus.They sought to create a sisterhood that would embrace and celebrate cultural diversity, and that was rooted in the shared principles of honesty, loyalty, respect, open-mindedness, leadership, and academic excellence.Since its founding, Sigma Theta Psi has remained a sisterhood unparalleled by any other. The multicultural sorority is a well-organized society of dedicated and goal-oriented individuals, and continues to grow strong today.

name: Sikh Student Association
description: This organization shall be to serve as a hub for the Sikh students and other interested students of the academic community here at UC Merced to interact, discuss and practice the Sikh religion as well as give its members the opportunity to represent the Sikh religion to the greater community in the city of Merced as well as the University. Members will take part in community service events, raising awareness and educating, activities, tabling events, and more.

name: SnowCats
description: The UC Merced SnowCats Club brings together students who share an interest in skiing, snowboarding, and outdoor winter recreation. The organization aims to provide opportunities for students of all skill levels to connect, develop their skills, and participate in organized activities and trips to destinations such as Lake Tahoe and Mammoth Mountain. The club also seeks to make skiing and snowboarding more accessible to students who are new to the sports by providing a supportive community where members can learn from one another. As the organization develops.

name: Social Creatives Club
description: The Social Creatives Club (SCC) is established to introduce and promote digital creation, encompassing brand ambassadorships, influencing, and digital content creation. The club's objectives include building connections among UC Merced members interested in digital creation, providing resources for personal and professional growth, sharing influencing strategies, and facilitating collaborations with similar communities and platforms while strictly avoiding involvement in fraudulent activities like pyramid schemes or multi-level marketing. Through networking events, workshops, and partnerships, IHC empowers its members to engage in ethical and legal collaborative ventures, enhancing their creative pursuits and career development within the digital creation space.

name: Society for Advancement of Chicanos/Hispanics and Native Americans in Science
description: SACNAS at UC Merced is a national inclusive organization dedicated to fostering the success of Hispanic/Chicanos and Native Americans, from college students to professionals to attain advanced degrees, careers, and positions of leadership in science. We make sure to support and develop the best version of our members. Striving to increase the number of minorities in the STEM field and overall Science Fields.

name: Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics
description: The purpose of SIAM at UC Merced shall be to advance the application of mathematics and computational science to engineering, industry, science, and society as well as promote research and facilitate the exchange of ideas in those areas. The student chapter aims to invite prominent speakers, highlight the research of the UC Merced students in mathematics, engineering and science, and promote mathematics, science, education and diversity at UC Merced and the surrounding communities.

name: Society of Asian Scientists & Engineers
description: SASE is a non-profit student organization dedicated to help advance scientists & engineers of (and not limited to) Asian heritage for success after their undergraduate degree though the development of one’s professional/technical skills, providing opportunities to individuals, surrounding students with a network of individuals that want them to succeed, and to promote/celebrate diversity on campus. Our vision statement is to have each one of our members set up with a variety of professional experiences to allow them to transition to life after their undergraduate degree effortlessly, whether that be to help them attain an internship, research position, etc.

name: Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers
description: The purpose of this student chapter is to increase the number of Hispanic STEM students at the University of California, Merced. Promote the advancement of Hispanic engineers and scientists in employment and education. Develop and participate in programs within the industry and the university, which benefit students seeking technical degrees. Improve the retention of Hispanic students enrolled in engineering and science. Provide a forum for the exchange of information pertinent for Hispanic engineering/science students enrolled at UC Merced. Increase STEM Awareness towards Hispanic students in and around Merced County.

name: Society of Physics Students
description: The Society of Physics Students (SPS) is a professional association explicitly designed for students and their advisers. Membership, through collegiate chapters, is open to anyone interested in physics. The only requirement for membership is that you be interested in physics. Besides physics majors, our members can include majors in astronomy, chemistry, computer science, engineering, geology, mathematics, medicine, and other fields. SPS is open to everyone.Purpose and MissionSPS is a chapter based society that exists to help students transform themselves into contributing members of the professional community. Traditional coursework develops only one range of skills. Other skills needed to flourish professionally include effective communication and personal interactions, leadership experience, establishing a personal network of contacts, presenting scholarly work in professional meetings and journals, research experiences, and outreach services to the campus and local communities. Through its members, advisers, chapters, and leadership, SPS enables national initiatives and local impacts within the community. SPS supports students, advisers, and departments to improve the overall community.HistoryThe Society of Physics Students was formed in 1968 with a constitution that combined its two "parent" organizations. SPS now has over 820 chapters on campuses across the country.

name: Society of Women Engineers
description: SWE at UC Merced is a professional organization that works together to bring support to female engineers on campus. Our members gain valuable knowledge and insight into today's job markets by attending both local workshops and national conferences. Our goal is to help every member achieve maximum professional and educational success.SWE at UC Merced acknowledges the importance of outreach and encouraging younger students to pursue careers in engineering through the annual conference (EYH) for middle school and high school students. Through the conference, the students participate in workshops that enhance their knowledge of engineering.

name: Sociology Club
description: Hi everyone! Thank you for your interest in the Sociology Club at UC Merced. The purpose of our club is to prepare sociology majors and minors for their upcoming careers, graduate school, and support your in your coursework throughout the semester. Our club meetings center around professional development and include topics such as time management, career panels, graduate school application prep, and more! We also want to help sociology students get to know one another, so we have some social events planned as well, such as a halloween movie night and a game night! Come by and join us!The Sociology Club is organized to provide a foundation of support for sociology majors and minors through:organizing activities pertaining to graduate school and careers in sociologycreating opportunities for students interested in sociology to meet each otherencouraging interaction among faculty and studentsintegrating a forum for relevant activities in the communitysharing experiences through a sociological perspective and inspiring more students to pursue education in sociology.

name: Sociology Graduate Student Committee
description: The purpose of SGSC is to facilitate collaboration among the Sociology Graduate community, provide experience in higher education service work, foster a professional atmosphere among members, and instill professional pride in the sociological sciences. It is also to foster professor/student relationships through the inclusion of graduate students in department activities.

name: Soulaan Student Society
description: The Soulaan Student Society. The purpose of this society is to empower Black and African American students by celebrating their cultural heritage, highlighting their historical and present-day importance in America, and creating a true home on campus where their voices, contributions, and identities are recognized and uplifted.

name: South Asian Student Association
description: South Asian Student Association is deeply in UC Merced. The club started when the school was only a couple of years old and that makes us one of the oldest clubs on campus. Our goal is to provide a safe place for students who are passionate about South Asian culture to explore and experience the culture. We strive to illuminate the beautiful South Asian culture across campus. Now that we are in person it is finally time to make this a possibility again. Currently, the club focuses on doing socials and hosting large cultural events on campus. We will be having two main events this year which is HOLI and Bollywood Bash. Our socials will range from Bollywood movie nights, and the Pani Puri Competition to everything else in between. A big part of South Asian culture is to give back to our community so we will be doing just that. There will be several community service opportunities from lake clean-up to a food drive.

name: Stars of Hope
description: Stars of Hope is a pediatric based oncology club at UC Merced dedicated to raising awareness about pediatric cancer, supporting young patients and their families, and fostering a community of students passionate about oncology and healthcare. Our mission is to educate, advocate, and engage in service projects that make a meaningful impact on children battling cancer. Through education, outreach, and community service, we aim to inspire the next generation of healthcare professionals to make a difference in the lives of children with cancer. Join us in our efforts to bring hope and support to young cancer patients and their families while advancing knowledge in pediatric oncology.

name: Student Alumni Association
description: UC Merced Student Alumni Association (SAA) strives to leave a legacy and prepare students for their future role as alumni. SAA members aim to connect current students to alumni through networking opportunities, cultivate a culture of philanthropy throughout the university and encourages participation in UC Merced traditions that make you a part of the Bobcat Family.

name: Student Filmmakers Association
description: The Student Filmmakers Association is a vibrant and creative community where aspiring filmmakers come together to explore the art and craft of cinema. From script-writing and directing to cinematography and editing, our club offers a platform for members to collaborate, learn, and bring their cinematic visions to life while fostering a passion for storytelling through the lens. Whether you're a seasoned filmmaker or a novice looking to embark on a cinematic journey, our club provides a welcoming space to nurture your talents, share ideas, and produce compelling films that captivate and inspire audiences. Join us in capturing the magic of storytelling on the silver screen!

name: Students for Justice in Palestine
description: Founded in 2023, Students for Justice in Palestine at UC Merced demands justice for the Palestinian people and accountability from our institutions. We strive to cultivate a thriving community in solidarity with Palestinians and against colonialism.

name: Students for Veterans
description: Students for Veterans is a student-led organization dedicated to supporting veterans through service, advocacy, and community engagement. Our mission focuses on challenges veterans may face, including housing insecurity, limited access to essential resources, and social isolation. By partnering with local organizations, we organize fundraising campaigns, hygiene/toiletry drives, food and clothing donations as well as community events that directly benefit veterans and local shelters. Through these efforts, we aim to honor veterans’ service and make a meaningful difference in the communities they call home.

name: Students United for Reproductive and Gender Equity @ UC Merced
description: URGE envisions a liberated world where we can live with justice, love freely, express our gender and sexuality, and define and create families of our choosing.URGE centers the leadership of young people 18-30 years old who are Black, Indigenous, and other people of color, women, queer, trans, nonbinary, and people working to make ends meet, and infuses Reproductive Justice principles and values throughout our work. Working across the progressive landscape, URGE works together to build strong communities where sexual health is valued, Reproductive Justice is sacrosanct, and each body is celebrated and supported.As a state-driven national organization, URGE organizes our communities, provides a political home for young people, advocates for meaningful policy change, and shifts culture, working in states where the challenges and opportunities are greatest.

name: Super Smash Brother's Club
description: This club is here to provide a safe and sustainable environment for everyone that has an interest in Super Smash Brothers. This club is a perfect way to relieve some stress and socialize with your peers. We are open to any and all players, whether you prefer casual or competitive play. Whether you're trying to learn the game, practice your skills, or even just watch; our doors are wide open for you! The best thing is that it's completely free!We have nearly biweekly tourneys on Saturdays and Fridays! Stay tuned on our Instagram: @ucmsmashbros and our Discord Server!﻿

name: The Basketball Club
description: The purpose of TBC is to unite the community through shared interests in basketball, encouraging connections and providing opportunities for individuals to bond through the game. TBC aims to establish and maintain an active community of basketball players who are focused on enjoying the sport in a fun and inclusive environment. TBC will positively impact the university community by offering incoming students a platform to build relationships, network, and easily form friendships through participation in basketball.

name: The Biomedical Engineering Society
description: The purpose of the Biomedical Engineering Society (BMES) Student Chapter is to encourage the development, dissemination, integration, and utilization of knowledge in biomedical engineering through means of research, discussion, and application. The chapter promotes community through the provision and insight of the objectives of BMES via networking and outreach opportunities within the university's department and external relations.

name: The Business Society
description: Established in 2005 at the first American research institution built in the 21st century, the Business Society strives to introduce and further knowledge about the professional world and how to stake your claim in it. Through a rigid command structure and high expectations, the Business Society at the University of California Merced is professionalism at its best.

name: The Chemistry Society
description: The Chemistry Society at UC Merced is a student-run organization focused on the professional success of our members in any field related to the chemical sciences through professional advancement and leadership growth. As a student chapter of the American Chemical Society (ACS), the Chemistry Society at UC Merced will foster professional growth and opportunity through workshops, outreach events, info sessions, and presentations of chemical science technology and careers.Founded in 1876 and chartered by the U.S. Congress, the American Chemical Society is one of the world's largest scientific organizations. We are devoted to furthering the advance of the broader chemistry enterprise along with all practitioners for the benefit of the earth and its people. Through the transforming power of chemistry, we seek to improve the lives of all.To stay up on club events and happenings join the conversation on DISCORD: https://discord.gg/xYSfhXKpv3

name: The Creative Writing, Literature, and Poetry Club
description: We are The Creative Writing, Literature, and Poetry Club. Our club meets weekly for an hour with the aim of providing a warm social space where members can develop their self-expression by sharing original work and collaborating across all forms of creative writing and literature. From poetry and short stories to songwriting and everything in between, we aim to support, inspire, and strengthen all the pen wielders in the UCMerced community!

name: The Fusion Club
description: The purpose(s) of this organization shall be to act as the foremost organization in offering UC Merced students opportunities that expose them to the field of fusion research. The Fusion Club’s organization will focus on the development of its flagship project, a functioning fusion reactor located at UC Merced. The project will engage the campus research community (professors, post-docs, graduate students, undergraduates) to achieve this goal. Firstly, the reasoning is to push UC Merced towards participating in world class fusion science research. Secondly, to enable its members to experience challenges on the level of real professional level innovation, offering them a steppingstone towards graduate school and industry. The club strongly supports cooperation between a diverse set of students to enable innovative ideas and accelerate progress.

name: The Golden Crumb at UC Merced
description: We, the members of The Golden Crumb at UC Merced, established this club to foster a collaborative and inclusive environment where students can develop baking skills, explore creativity, and build community through shared culinary experiences!

name: The Historical Society
description: The Historical Society is a collective campus club that aims to bring together students in the History Department, as well as students interested in History as a whole. The University community will be able to gather and unite to discuss topics within the field, as well as topics surrounding the history field. There is an emphasis on collaboration and exploration within the Historical Society, and the club is a space for students to work alongside like-minded individuals.

name: The Human Help Project at UC Merced
description: The Human Help Project is designed to help people, help people. With the support of UCM students and staff, we hope to empower other organizations and clubs on campus to give back to their community. Our goal is to give back to those who could benefit from additional support, not just in Merced but across California. Most importantly, we want to inspire and motivate all on the UCM campus to go out and cultivate a greater Merced. We believe that as our college town grows and the local economy prospers, we cannot forget the low-income families and the houseless people that we share our beautiful town with. We want to enrich those in need and make sure they are known that are seen and loved by our UCM family

name: The National Society of Leadership and Success at UC Merced
description: The National Society of Leadership and Success (NSLS) is the largest collegiate leadership development program in the United States, partnering with over 800 colleges and universities and engaging more than 2 million members. Through accredited leadership development programming, NSLS equips students with the skills, confidence, and resources to achieve their goals and make a positive impact in their communities.At UC Merced, our organization aims to provide students with the opportunity to earn leadership certificates, gain recognition through a nationally affiliated leadership society, and engage in a structured, goal-oriented leadership development experience. Members will complete the Foundations of Leadership certificate, earning two widely recognized digital badges that can be showcased on resumes and LinkedIn profiles to enhance career opportunities.Beyond the certificate, NSLS members will have access to exclusive leadership summits, held both virtually and in person, allowing them to expand their professional networks by connecting with fellow leaders from campuses across the country. Additionally, our chapter is committed to service-oriented leadership, organizing community engagement projects throughout the academic year to foster meaningful impact both on campus and beyond.Our mission aligns with that of the NSLS: "We build leaders who make a better world." Through leadership training, networking opportunities, and service initiatives, we strive to empower UC Merced students to lead with integrity, purpose, and lasting influence.

name: The Pawsitive Project, UC Merced's Animal Support Initiative
description: The Pawsitive Project is a student-led club dedicated to improving animal welfare and supporting pet owners in our community. The club partners with local animal shelters, veterinary clinics, and non-profit organizations to provide hands-on volunteer opportunities and host educational workshops on responsible pet care. Members participate in both service-oriented workdays and social events, fostering a community of compassionate students who are committed to making a positive impact for animals and their owners.

name: The Phantom Troupe
description: Our Goal is to create a community between people who like anime by safely hosting a place where people can talk, read, and watch anime together by allowing members to vote on which anime we will watch every other week. The goal isn't simply to watch anime together, but to create a community. Therefore we host an activity every other week!The activities will include: Karaoke night, Art Night, Homework Night, Debate Night, Easter Egg Hunt, Day of the Dead Altar making, Valentines Day cookie making,  AND MORE!!

name: The Photography Club
description: The Photography Club exists as a resource for students that attend UC Merced that is centered in photography. The Photography Club wishes to help students to explore their interest in the art of photography as well as to provide a space for students to socialize with each other.

name: The Prestige
description: The Prestige, UC Merced's only student-run news publication! At the forefront of campus journalism, we are dedicated to bringing you the latest news, insightful commentary, and engaging stories that capture the heart and soul of our campus. Whether you're a student, faculty member, alumni, or simply curious about life at UC Merced, our platform is your window into the diverse experiences, achievements, and voices that shape our university.Email us: ﻿ucmnewspaper@gmail.com﻿

name: The Reading Club
description: The purpose of this organization shall be to create an engaging space for all members to explore new books and grow together through shared reading. As members of the club, we shall strive to find books that suit all members of the organization to introduce new literature and promote reading.In particular, we plan on reading a book a month per recommendation from a member. We plan on reaching out to the local community of Merced through local literary leaders.

name: The Vernal Pool
description: The Vernal Pool, with support of the Global Arts, Media, and Writing Studies Program, focuses on the practical approaches to editing The Vernal Pool, UC Merced’s undergraduate literary journal. Students coordinate the journal’s editorial flow and manage stages of submission. Students engage author inquiries and editorial board suggestions for sustainably producing the journal, engaging a range of content, layout, and ethical concerns for publication. Individuals interested in joining the Vernal Pool Editorial Board must be registered for WRI 131B (Journal Production: The Vernal Pool) and WRI 131A (Journal Production: Technical Writing and Editing) as a co-requisite or prerequisite.

name: The Whimsical Workshop: Crafting Club
description: Welcome to The Whimsical Workshop, a cozy corner where creativity runs free! We're a crafting club built on the belief that everyone deserves a space to explore, imagine, and create; without judgment, pressure, or perfection. We celebrate whimsy in all its forms; playful ideas, happy accidents, and the joy of making something just because it makes you smile. Our workshop is a safe and inclusive environment where every voice is heard and every project, no matter how big or small, is worth celebrating.

name: Theta Tau
description: Theta Tau is a professional engineering fraternity that was established in 1904. Since becoming a chapter at UC Merced in 2012 the organization has worked to help develop future engineers for a successful future in the field after college. With many leadership and learning opportunities, Theta Tau gives future engineers a place to grow into their professional selves. Our pillars are Service, Profession, and Brotherhood.

name: Tiny Health Tales
description: Health literacy and public awareness about common health problems are critical for individual and public health. The San Joaquin Valley of California, home to four million people, is a medically underserved region with a severe lack of access to healthcare and resources, contributing to the region’s high prevalence of health concerns. In response to individuals' health education challenges in the medically underserved region of the San Joaquin Valley (SJV) in California, our organization hopes to use animated medical education videos as a supplementary learning tool regarding health education.

name: Trading Card Game Club
description: Trading Card Game Club will meet weekly on Thursday evenings and hopes to create a safe space for people of all backgrounds and card games to come together and have fun together. Whether you are a casual player or a tournament grinder, there will be someone with the same objectives to play with! Support all card games, including but not limited to; Magic the Gathering, Vanguard, Yu-Gi-Oh, WiXoss, Digimon, and more!

name: Transfer, Returning, Veteran Student Services
description: Transfer, Returning and Veteran (TRV) Student Services supports transfer, returning, and veteran students through their integration, transition, and degree attainment while at UC Merced.  TRV Student Services understands and values the unique experiences and perspectives non-traditional students bring to our vibrant campus community. The mission of TRV Student Services is to celebrate the diversity of our students and to assist in the discovery of services available to UC Merced students. TRV accomplishes this mission by offering individual, academic, and community support as well as advocacy, resources referrals and career exploration.  We also provide several social and academic events throughout the semester to help foster a sense of community and camaraderie with fellow Transfer, Returning and Veteran Students.

name: Trenzas Sin Fronteras
description: This organization strives to primarily establish fundraising opportunities to donate to preexisting charities that provide services to families and communities affected by the political state of the world.

name: Turning Point USA
description: Through guest speakers, campus events, tabling, and discussions, we strive to create an environment where students can exchange ideas respectfully, build lasting connections, and encourage active participation in the democratic process. Membership is open to all UC Merced students regardless of political affiliation.

name: UC Merced Extension
description: What is Extension?UC Merced Extension offers access to the university's academic courses through Open University and provides professional courses in a variety of industry fields (education, business, technology, renewable energy, healthcare, etc.). UC Merced Extension partners with regional community intiatives and organizations to boost economic and social development with a focus on delivering courses in convenient and flexible formats, including fully online, hybrid, in-person, and custom modalities.UC Merced Extension offers workforce-responsive, non-degree credentials and credential pathways that provide opportunities to upskill and re-skill. We can develop and deliver skills-based, alternative credential programs that align with employer needs and high demand jobs. Alternative credentials are non-degree, professional credit, certificate, stackable, micro-credentials, bootcamps, etc.

name: UC Merced Men's Soccer Club
description: Our Competitive Soccer Club is dedicated to providing student-athletes with the opportunity to continue playing soccer at a high level while representing our university. The purpose of the club is to create a competitive environment where players can develop their skills, compete against other universities and colleges, and stay committed to the sport beyond recreational play.

name: UC Merced Swim Club
description: The UC Merced swim club's goal to become an NCAA team for UCM in the future! Don't be intimidated however, we have a recreational and competitive group and hope to see you at the pool with us! We aim to foster personal development, health, and sportsmanship through regular training, educational workshops, and community events. If any of those interest you then consider reaching out and joining our community!To join our club and be cleared for practice please fill out this google form (https://forms.gle/m6odzCLPyjuqpZ5o9 if you want to copy and paste it) to get some basic information about you. We will use it to add you to our club's roster and to get you the clearance/compliance forms so you attend practice. Please join our Discord, follow us on Instagram, or shoot us an email if you have any questions!

name: UCM Archery Club
description: The purpose of the collegiate archery team is to represent the University of California, Merced in competitive local, state, regional, and national archery tournaments and competitions. This competitive club has been established to promote and develop skills in archery. The UC Merced Archery team will coach and provide a place for anyone ranging from interested to experienced in archery.Officers:President: Matthew LezhanskyVice-President/Safety Officer: Diego AlonsoSecretary: Vincent TrinhTreasurer: Melissa Burns
regularMeetingTime: Saturday: 11 AM - 2 PM, Sunday: 11 AM - 2 PM

name: UCM Beyblade club
description: The Beyblade club is an organization that helps students socialize through beyblading, for those who do not know, Beyblade is a customizable spinning top toy used for competitive or casual head-to-head battles inside an arena called a Beystadium. We welcome all members, whether they are new or experienced beybladers, and incase anyone doesn't own any beyblades, no worries! we have some that our members can borrow to play with.The main communication for this club is through discord. Here is the link https://discord.gg/XTmKU3Abj

name: UCM Cheer Team
description: Hello Bobcats! Our cheerleading (co-ed) team consists of an Elite Team (competition team) and a Pep Team. If an individual makes the team, they are automatically placed on our Pep Team. Once they are evaluated and are interested in joining the Elite Team, their skills and efforts are evaluated by the E-Board members of UCM Cheer. If you have any questions, comments, or concerns please email ucmcheer@ucmerced.edu.President: Evelin Esteban Vice President : Angelina Jones Secretary: Amayah GonzalesTreasurer: Amira MuhammadSafety Officer: Mercedes San-Nicolas

name: UCM Dance Team
description: The UC Merced Bobcat Dance Team, established in 2009, is known by the university student body to perform dance routines, and cheer during sporting games and other school events. During practices, the members strive to improve their dance technique, musicality, and performance quality. Outside of practice, the team performs in parades and volunteers within the Merced community. Throughout the dance season, the team prepares for an annual national competition in the spring, in which they compete with collegiate dance teams from across the country. The UC Merced Dance Team continues to strive for overall improvement to be a team that members are excited to be a part of and the university is proud to have!

name: UCM Ritmo Latino
description: At UC Merced, our Latin dance group is more than just a performance team—it is a community where culture, creativity, and personal growth come together.
