We showcase a variety of dance styles from across Latin America, using movement not only to entertain but also to tell meaningful stories that celebrate and preserve the beauty of Latin American traditions. Our goal is to create a welcoming space where every member can feel confident, explore different styles of dance, and even learn skills like makeup and hair that are part of the performance experience. But beyond the stage, dance is about growth. It teaches discipline, teamwork, and creativity, while also helping you build leadership skills and self-expression. Through learning the history and cultural context behind each style, members gain a deeper appreciation for the diversity of Latin America, its people, and its traditions. Most importantly, our group is a family. We support one another, make lasting friendships, and create memories that go far beyond rehearsals and performances. Whether you are an experienced dancer or a complete beginner, joining us means stepping into a vibrant community where culture comes alive and every story is told through the power of dance.

name: UCM Softball Club
description: As the 2019 Pacific Region, Central Conference, Champions, UC Merced’s Softball team is looking to continue it’s hard hitting streak. The club takes pride in creating a safe, fun and positive environment for women who wish to continue playing softball competitively at a collegiate level.Whether you're a seasoned veteran or new to the game, our club provides a supportive platform for growth, skill development, and personal achievement. We believe in the power of sport to bring people together, and we actively encourage friendship and mutual respect among our members.

name: UCM Tennis Club
description: ﻿The purpose of the collegiate tennis team is to represent the University of California, Merced in competitive local, regional, and national tennis tournaments hosted by the United States Tennis Association (USTA) Tennis on Campus (TOC). The tennis club will provide a place for anyone ranging from the beginner to advanced level in tennis. Given the competitive and physical nature of Tennis, improving in this sport requires determination and dedication from members, and is time consuming. Coaching will be provided from time to time but it will NOT be guaranteed.
regularMeetingLocation: On Campus Tennis Courts (Behind Glacier Point)

name: Undergraduate Research Journal
description: For over a decade, the UC Merced Undergraduate Research Journal has gathered, polished, and published the best research produced by our students across the academic disciplines. Founded in 2007 by UCM Merritt Writing Program faculty, the URJ (as the journal is colloquially known) is produced twice per academic year by students enrolled in Writing 131C, a professional editing and journal production course. In the interests of furthering the spread of knowledge, the URJ is an open-access publication indexed in the Directory of Open Access Journals; in other words, there is no paywall or subscription fee separating our content from potential readers. We invite submissions from students across our campus in the heart of California's Central Valley, and we attract readers from all over the world.

name: University Honors Club
description: The University Honors Club (UHC) at UC Merced is a student-led organization dedicated to encouraging academic excellence, intellectual growth, and community support among students of all backgrounds and disciplines. UHC provides opportunities for leadership development, service involvement, professional growth, and peer connection beyond the classroom. The club works to connect members with campus resources, scholarships, internships, and research opportunities while creating an encouraging and collaborative environment where students can thrive academically and personally. Through monthly meetings, events, and service projects, UHC helps members strengthen their skills, expand their networks, and contribute positively to the UC Merced community.

name: Valley Lung Initiative
description: Valley Lung Initiative is a student organization at UC Merced dedicated to advancing respiratory health education in California's San Joaquin Valley. The region ranks among the most polluted air basins in the United States, and children here experience elevated rates of asthma and related respiratory conditions. Trained undergraduate volunteers visit middle schools across the Valley to lead a single class period lesson on lung function and air quality, followed by a hands on activity in which students build a working model of the respiratory system. Programming is offered at no cost to participating schools. The organization welcomes volunteers from all academic backgrounds, and prior teaching experience is not required. Advised by Dr. Adeyemi Adebiyi, Life and Environmental Sciences.

name: Vanguard Engineering Society
description: Vanguard Engineering Society is a student-run umbrella organization underneath the  School of Engineering whose vision is to build an engineering community of leaders focused on the professional and technical development of their peers,  UC Merced, and the local community. We make this possible by executing our daily mission of supporting the development of engineering registered club organizations (RCOs) by preparing every student leader with the foundations in leadership and impact-driven strategies.

name: VIDA Volunteer Organization
description: VIDA Volunteer is an organization that gives students the opportunity to gain medical clinical hours by hosting trips to regions without sufficient access to health care. Students work with doctors to learn how to diagnose, take vitals, diagnose, and create treatment plans. At the end of the trip, students are rewarded with a certificate and letter from the organization stating the number of hours worked in the clinics. https://www.vidavolunteer.org is the official website for the organization. By joining VIDA Volunteer at UC Merced, students can join in on several sub-projects hosted by the club. Some projects include spreading awareness on campus of preventable diseases. MCAT study sessions are additionally hosted for pre-med students.

name: Vietnamese Student Association
description: At VSA, we strive to promote the general welfare of the Vietnamese community by allowing our members to have a better understanding of what the Vietnamese culture is. Although we are a cultural organization, we emphasize the importance in other aspects such as academics and being integrated within the UC Merced community as well.Many events are held throughout the year to spread appreciation and knowledge about the Vietnamese culture. The many events VSA hold and attend, but are not limited to, are: Mid-Autumn Festival, Anh Chi Em (A.C.E.), NorCal UVSA Summit, Lunar New Year, and Culture Show.

name: Visioneers
description: Visioneers is all about creativity. We want to create a space that encourages artistic exploration, supports original ideas, and helps students connect through collaboration. Our projects blend engineering, music, illusions, and animation to create immersive art that brings imagination to life. No engineering background is needed, just curiosity, creativity, and a sense of fun.

name: Women in Science
description: The goal of Women in Science is to advance the representation, recognition, and leadership of women in scientific and professional spaces by fostering an inclusive, supportive community that promotes professional development and career advancement for women graduate students and their allies. Through seminars, social events, outreach activities, and community-building initiatives, we aim to provide opportunities, resources, and connections that: (1) bring together, support, and uplift women in science; (2) foster professional growth and support women in achieving their goals throughout their careers; and (3) empower women to pursue and attain leadership positions across government, academia, and industry.

name: Yamabuki Taiko
description: Yamabuki Taiko is a club dedicated to learning the art of Japanese drumming taiko through weekly practices where students are taught the basics of taiko alongside songs.

name: Yosemite Leadership Program
description: This two-year experience integrates training in leadership skills, education on the theories and practices of leadership, and personal and professional development opportunities to create generations of socially engaged and environmentally aware global stewards.The Yosemite Leadership Program (YLP) is one arm of a larger collaborative effort between UC Merced and the National Park Service to proactively address the challenges of the 21st century.  UC Merced students in YLP are helping address the leadership needs of parks, public lands and the environment, now and into the future.

name: Young Artists' Movement
description: Young Artists' Movement is UC Merced's first and only student-led art coalition. We are committed to sustaining an artistic climate on campus that allows self-expression, visual culture-oriented education, and social activism to flourish. All students from all artistic backgrounds are welcome, regardless of talent or experience.

name: Young Democratic Socialists of America
description: YDSA is a student political organization meant to help organize workers and teach students about the ideas of democratic socialism. Our goal as an organization is to be politically involved within Merced, the Greater Central Valley, and surrounding regions, to spread information and awareness of democratic socialism, and to help organize workers with emphasis on undocumented workers. Our primary purpose above all else is to organize young people and integrate them with the goals and objectives of DSA (Democratic Socialists of America).

name: Younglife College UC Merced
description: Every UC Merced student is seeking community, adventure, and significance. We believe the remedy is a student leadership team deeply committed to Jesus Christ, living in genuine friendship with one another, and boldly inviting the lost and lonely into the family of God. We hope to reach the unreached, build them up in their faith, and launch them into a life of discipleship beyond their years on campus.

name: Youth Advisory Council
description: The purpose of the Youth Advisory Council is to provide the space for students tobe educated on the stimulant & opioid crisis, through a series of workshops,trainings, given by current officers or outside organizations. While also being ableto obtain access to off campus support organizations. The organization shalloperate as a not-for-profit student organization, and all funds shall be used tofurther the organization’s educational and advocacy purposes.

name: Zen Garden Community Building Club
description: The Zen Garden Community Building Club, or the Zen Garden Club, is a community building and serving initiative. Through sharing food from UC Merced's Community Garden, as well as other partners, collaborating with on-campus resources, hosting community-building activities, and beautify underutilized or overlooked spaces on campus, we strive to cultivate a culture of service, sustainability, and community engagement among UC Merced students.
